decisions.choice: a new speech, to Moses and Aaron together: the laws on skin disease and on mold in cloth
decisions.reason: Aaron is addressed with Moses, as in 11:1 and 15:1, because the priests are the ones who apply these laws: in every case the priest looks and gives the ruling. The speech runs to the end of the chapter (verse 59).

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("parla", "dit"); passé composé at Readable ("a dit")
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets for narrative: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative, the passé composé the tense readers use today. The laws that follow are in the future (Literal, Balanced) or with "doit" (Readable).

source.text: אָדָ֗ם כִּֽי־יִהְיֶ֤ה בְעוֹר־בְּשָׂרוֹ֙ שְׂאֵ֤ת אֽוֹ־סַפַּ֨חַת֙ א֣וֹ בַהֶ֔רֶת וְהָיָ֥ה בְעוֹר־בְּשָׂר֖וֹ לְנֶ֣גַע צָרָ֑עַת וְהוּבָא֙ אֶל־אַהֲרֹ֣ן הַכֹּהֵ֔ן א֛וֹ אֶל־אַחַ֥ד מִבָּנָ֖יו הַכֹּהֲנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] person, when will be on [the] skin of his flesh [a] swelling or [a] scab or [a] bright spot, and it becomes on [the] skin of his flesh [a] mark of scale disease, and he will be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons the priests.

en.L: "A person, when there is on the skin of his flesh a swelling or a scab or a bright spot, and it becomes a mark of scale disease on the skin of his flesh, then he shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.
en.B: "If a swelling, a scab or a bright spot appears on the skin of someone's body and turns into what may be a sore of serious skin disease, the person is to be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.
en.R: "Someone may get a swelling, a scab or a shiny spot on their skin. If it begins to look like a sore from a serious skin disease, the person must be taken to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who serve as priests.

es.L: «Cuando una persona tenga en la piel de su carne una hinchazón, o una costra, o una mancha brillante, y se convierta en la piel de su carne en marca de enfermedad de la piel, será llevada a Aarón el sacerdote o a uno de sus hijos, los sacerdotes.
es.B: «Si en la piel del cuerpo de alguien aparece una hinchazón, una costra o una mancha brillante, y se convierte en lo que puede ser una llaga de enfermedad grave de la piel, esa persona será llevada al sacerdote Aarón o a uno de sus hijos, los sacerdotes.
es.R: «Puede que a alguien le salga en la piel una hinchazón, una costra o una mancha que brilla. Si empieza a parecer la llaga de una enfermedad grave de la piel, hay que llevar a esa persona a Aarón el sacerdote o a uno de sus hijos que sirven como sacerdotes.

fr.L: « Quand quelqu’un aura sur la peau de sa chair une enflure, ou une croûte, ou une tache brillante, et que cela deviendra sur la peau de sa chair une marque de maladie de peau, il sera amené à Aaron le prêtre ou à l’un de ses fils, les prêtres.
fr.B: « Si une enflure, une croûte ou une tache brillante apparaît sur la peau de quelqu’un et devient ce qui pourrait être une lésion de maladie de peau grave, on amènera cette personne à Aaron le prêtre ou à l’un de ses fils, les prêtres.
fr.R: « Il peut arriver qu’une personne ait sur la peau une enflure, une croûte ou une tache qui brille. Si cela commence à ressembler à la plaie d’une maladie de peau grave, il faut amener cette personne à Aaron le prêtre ou à l’un de ses fils qui sont prêtres.

sw.L: "Mtu atakapokuwa na uvimbe, au kigaga, au doa linalong'aa katika ngozi ya mwili wake, nalo likawa katika ngozi ya mwili wake alama ya ugonjwa wa ngozi, ataletwa kwa Haruni kuhani au kwa mmoja wa wanawe, makuhani.
sw.B: "Mtu akitokwa na uvimbe, kigaga au doa linalong'aa kwenye ngozi ya mwili wake, nalo likageuka kuwa kitu kinachoweza kuwa kidonda cha ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi, mtu huyo ataletwa kwa Haruni kuhani au kwa mmoja wa wanawe, makuhani.
sw.R: "Huenda mtu akapata uvimbe, kigaga au doa linalong'aa kwenye ngozi yake. Likianza kuonekana kama kidonda cha ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi, lazima mtu huyo apelekwe kwa Haruni kuhani au kwa mmoja wa wanawe wanaotumika kama makuhani.

decisions.choice: scale disease: a group of skin conditions that made a person unclean, not modern leprosy
decisions.reason: The word names skin conditions with visible signs: swellings, scabs or flaking, white spots, raw flesh, hair turning white (verses 3-44). Leprosy as known today (Hansen's disease) does not fit these signs well, and the same word is used of a growth in cloth or leather (verse 47) and in the walls of a house (14:34). The law treats it as a matter of uncleanness more than of health: the priest rules on it, and the person lives outside the camp (verse 46). The Greek Septuagint renders it with the word from which 'leprosy' comes, and older translations followed it.

decisions.choice: mark: a visible patch of disease, literally a 'touch' or 'stroke'
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb 'touch' or 'strike'. It can mean a blow or a plague (Exodus 11:1). In these chapters it is the mark of the disease on skin, cloth or wall, and in verses 4, 12, 13, 17 and 31 it stands for the person who has the mark.

decisions.choice: swelling, scab, bright spot: three first signs that may or may not be the disease
decisions.reason: The swelling is literally a 'rising', a raised place on the skin. The scab is a crust or flaking patch; a related word names a harmless one in verses 6-8. The bright spot comes from a verb meaning to shine: a white, glossy patch (verse 4). None of them is unclean in itself; the person is brought to the priest because they may turn out to be the disease. The same three are listed in the summary at 14:56.

decisions.choice: a sore of serious skin disease
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one English term for each Hebrew word, 'mark' and 'scale disease', so a reader can follow them through chapters 13 and 14 and see that the same words cover cloth and houses. Balanced and Readable say 'sore' and 'serious skin disease', which say what is meant without suggesting modern leprosy.

decisions.choice: someone / the person / they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the general word for a human being, so the law is for men and women alike. Balanced and Readable say 'the person' or 'they' through the chapter where the Hebrew says 'he'; Literal keeps 'he'. Readable says 'shiny spot' for the bright spot, as in 14:56.

decisions.choice: "enfermedad de la piel" (L); "enfermedad grave de la piel" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Lepra", the traditional Spanish word, now means Hansen's disease, which these signs do not describe (see m1). Literal keeps one plain term for the Hebrew word through chapters 13 and 14, as in Exodus 4:6 and Numbers 12:10; Balanced and Readable add "grave", as the English says "serious".

decisions.choice: "marca" (L), "llaga" (B, R) for the mark; "hinchazón", "costra", "mancha brillante" (R "mancha que brilla")
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "marca" as the English keeps "mark", one word for skin, cloth and wall. Balanced and Readable say "llaga", the ordinary word for a sore on the skin. The three first signs keep these words through chapters 13 and 14.

decisions.choice: "maladie de peau" (L); "maladie de peau grave" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Lèpre", the traditional French word, now means Hansen's disease, which these signs do not describe (see m1). Literal keeps one plain term for the Hebrew word through chapters 13 and 14, as in Exodus 4:6 and Numbers 12:10; Balanced and Readable add "grave", as the English says "serious".

decisions.choice: "marque" (L), "lésion" (B), "plaie" (R) for the mark; "enflure", "croûte", "tache brillante" (R "tache qui brille")
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "marque" as the English keeps "mark", one word for skin, cloth and wall. Balanced says "lésion", which names a sore on the skin without suggesting a wound; Readable says "plaie", the everyday word. These words are used through chapters 13 and 14.

decisions.choice: "ugonjwa wa ngozi" (L); "ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Ukoma", the traditional Swahili word, now means Hansen's disease, which these signs do not describe (see m1). Literal keeps one plain term for the Hebrew word through chapters 13 and 14, as in Exodus 4:6 and Numbers 12:10; Balanced and Readable add "mbaya", as the English says "serious".

decisions.choice: "alama" (L), "kidonda" (B, R) for the mark; "uvimbe", "kigaga", "doa linalong'aa"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "alama" as the English keeps "mark", one word for skin, cloth and wall. Balanced and Readable say "kidonda", a sore. The three first signs keep these words through chapters 13 and 14.

source.text: וְרָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֣ן אֶת־הַנֶּ֣גַע בְּעֽוֹר־הַ֠בָּשָׂר וְשֵׂעָ֨ר בַּנֶּ֜גַע הָפַ֣ךְ׀לָבָ֗ן וּמַרְאֵ֤ה הַנֶּ֨גַע֙ עָמֹק֙ מֵע֣וֹר בְּשָׂר֔וֹ נֶ֥גַע צָרַ֖עַת ה֑וּא וְרָאָ֥הוּ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן וְטִמֵּ֥א אֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will see the priest the mark on [the] skin of the flesh, and hair in the mark has turned white, and [the] appearance of the mark [is] deep more than [the] skin of his flesh, [a] mark of scale disease it [is]; and will see him the priest and will pronounce unclean him.

en.L: And the priest shall look at the mark on the skin of the flesh, and [if] the hair in the mark has turned white and the appearance of the mark [is] deeper than the skin of his flesh, it [is] a mark of scale disease; and the priest shall look at him and pronounce him unclean.
en.B: The priest is to look closely at the sore. If the hair in it has turned white and it seems to go deeper than the surface of the skin, it is a sore of serious skin disease. Once he has seen it, the priest is to declare the person unclean.
en.R: The priest must look at the sore. The hair in it may have turned white, and the sore may seem to go deeper than the skin. Then it is a serious skin disease. After the priest looks at the person, he must say that the person is unclean.

es.L: Y el sacerdote mirará la marca en la piel de la carne; y [si] el pelo en la marca se ha vuelto blanco y el aspecto de la marca [es] más profundo que la piel de su carne, marca de enfermedad de la piel [es]; y el sacerdote lo mirará y lo declarará impuro.
es.B: El sacerdote examinará con atención la llaga. Si el pelo de la llaga se ha vuelto blanco y parece más honda que la superficie de la piel, es una llaga de enfermedad grave de la piel. Después de verla, el sacerdote declarará impura a la persona.
es.R: El sacerdote tiene que mirar la llaga. Tal vez el pelo que hay en ella se ha vuelto blanco, y la llaga parece más honda que la piel. Entonces es una enfermedad grave de la piel. Después de mirar a la persona, el sacerdote tiene que decir que es impura.

fr.L: Et le prêtre regardera la marque sur la peau de la chair ; et [si] le poil dans la marque est devenu blanc, et [si] l’aspect de la marque [est] plus profond que la peau de sa chair, c’[est] une marque de maladie de peau ; et le prêtre le regardera et le déclarera impur.
fr.B: Le prêtre examinera attentivement la lésion. Si le poil y est devenu blanc et qu’elle semble aller plus profond que la surface de la peau, c’est une lésion de maladie de peau grave. Après l’avoir examinée, le prêtre déclarera la personne impure.
fr.R: Le prêtre doit regarder la plaie. Les poils qui s’y trouvent sont peut-être devenus blancs, et la plaie semble peut-être plus profonde que la peau. Alors c’est une maladie de peau grave. Après avoir regardé la personne, le prêtre doit dire qu’elle est impure.

sw.L: Na kuhani ataiangalia alama katika ngozi ya mwili; na [ikiwa] nywele katika alama zimegeuka kuwa nyeupe, na sura ya alama [ni] ya ndani zaidi kuliko ngozi ya mwili wake, ni alama ya ugonjwa wa ngozi; na kuhani atamwangalia na kumtangaza kuwa najisi.
sw.B: Kuhani atakiangalia kidonda kwa makini. Ikiwa nywele zilizo ndani yake zimekuwa nyeupe, na kinaonekana kuingia ndani zaidi ya uso wa ngozi, ni kidonda cha ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi. Baada ya kukiona, kuhani atamtangaza mtu huyo kuwa najisi.
sw.R: Lazima kuhani akiangalie kidonda. Huenda nywele zilizo ndani yake zimekuwa nyeupe, na kidonda kinaonekana kuingia ndani zaidi ya ngozi. Basi ni ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi. Baada ya kumwangalia mtu huyo, lazima kuhani aseme kwamba yeye ni najisi.

decisions.choice: pronounce unclean: the priest rules that the person is unclean
decisions.reason: The verb is the strong form of 'be unclean', and here it means to declare or rule someone unclean, as its opposite in verse 6 means to declare clean. The priest does not cause the disease; his ruling settles the person's standing in the community, and from it they must live apart (verses 45-46). Telling the unclean from the clean is the priests' task (10:10).

decisions.choice: white hair: the hair growing in the mark has lost its color
decisions.reason: Hair that has turned white inside the mark is one of the two signs that it is the disease (also verses 10, 20, 25). In the hair of the head and beard the sign is thin yellow hair instead (verse 30), and black hair growing back shows healing (verse 37).

decisions.choice: deeper than the skin: the mark looks sunk below the surface
decisions.reason: The appearance is 'deep': it seems to lie below the skin around it rather than on top of it. Verse 20 uses a word meaning 'low' for the same sign. A mark that stays on the surface may be harmless (verse 4).

decisions.choice: declare unclean / say that the person is unclean
decisions.reason: Literal says 'pronounce', Balanced 'declare', and Readable 'say that ... is unclean'. Each makes clear that this is a ruling, used in the same way through chapters 13 and 14.

decisions.choice: "declarar impuro" (L, B); "decir que ... es impura" (R)
decisions.reason: The ruling is said as the English says it at each level, and in the same words through chapters 13 and 14, with "declarar puro" for its opposite.

decisions.choice: "déclarer impur" (L, B); "dire que ... est impure" (R); "le poil", "les poils" for the hair
decisions.reason: "Déclarer impur" is the natural French for a ruling, and is kept through chapters 13 and 14 with "déclarer pur" for its opposite. Hair growing on the skin is "poil" in French; "cheveux" would mean the hair of the head.

decisions.choice: "kumtangaza kuwa najisi" (L, B); "kusema kwamba ni najisi" (R)
decisions.reason: "Kutangaza", to announce, makes clear that the priest gives a public ruling. The same words are kept through chapters 13 and 14, with "kumtangaza kuwa safi" for its opposite.

source.text: וְאִם־בַּהֶרֶת֩ לְבָנָ֨ה הִ֜וא בְּע֣וֹר בְּשָׂר֗וֹ וְעָמֹק֙ אֵין־מַרְאֶ֣הָ מִן־הָע֔וֹר וּשְׂעָרָ֖ה לֹא־הָפַ֣ךְ לָבָ֑ן וְהִסְגִּ֧יר הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֶת־הַנֶּ֖גַע שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And if [a] bright spot white it [is] on [the] skin of his flesh, and deep not [is] its appearance more than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, then will shut up the priest the [one with the] mark seven days.

en.L: And if it [is] a white bright spot on the skin of his flesh, and its appearance [is] not deeper than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, then the priest shall shut up the [one with the] mark seven days.
en.B: If, however, there is a white bright spot on the skin that does not seem to go below the surface, and its hair has not turned white, the priest is to shut the person away for seven days.
en.R: But the shiny spot may be white without seeming to go deeper than the skin, and the hair in it may not have turned white. Then the priest must keep the person away from others for seven days.

es.L: Y si [hay] una mancha brillante blanca en la piel de su carne, y su aspecto no [es] más profundo que la piel, y su pelo no se ha vuelto blanco, el sacerdote encerrará [al que tiene] la marca siete días.
es.B: Pero si hay en la piel una mancha brillante blanca que no parece ir más allá de la superficie, y su pelo no se ha vuelto blanco, el sacerdote aislará a la persona durante siete días.
es.R: Pero la mancha que brilla puede ser blanca sin parecer más honda que la piel, y puede que el pelo que hay en ella no se haya vuelto blanco. Entonces el sacerdote tiene que mantener a la persona apartada de los demás durante siete días.

fr.L: Et si c’[est] une tache brillante blanche sur la peau de sa chair, et [si] son aspect n’[est] pas plus profond que la peau, et [si] son poil n’est pas devenu blanc, le prêtre enfermera [celui qui a] la marque sept jours.
fr.B: Si au contraire il y a sur la peau une tache brillante blanche qui ne semble pas s’enfoncer sous la surface, et dont le poil n’est pas devenu blanc, le prêtre isolera la personne pendant sept jours.
fr.R: Mais la tache qui brille peut être blanche sans sembler plus profonde que la peau, et les poils qui s’y trouvent ne sont peut-être pas devenus blancs. Alors le prêtre doit tenir la personne à l’écart des autres pendant sept jours.

sw.L: Na ikiwa ni doa jeupe linalong'aa katika ngozi ya mwili wake, na sura yake si ya ndani zaidi kuliko ngozi, na nywele zake hazijageuka kuwa nyeupe, kuhani atamfungia [mwenye] alama siku saba.
sw.B: Lakini ikiwa kuna doa jeupe linalong'aa kwenye ngozi ambalo halionekani kuingia chini ya uso wa ngozi, na nywele zake hazijawa nyeupe, kuhani atamtenga mtu huyo kwa siku saba.
sw.R: Lakini huenda doa linalong'aa likawa jeupe bila kuonekana kuingia ndani zaidi ya ngozi, na nywele zilizo ndani yake hazijawa nyeupe. Basi lazima kuhani amweke mtu huyo mbali na watu wengine kwa siku saba.

decisions.choice: shut up seven days: kept apart for a week so that the priest can see whether the mark changes
decisions.reason: The verb means to shut or close. Where the signs are not clear, the priest does not rule at once. He has the person kept apart and looks again after seven days, and if need be after a second week (verse 5). The person is not yet declared unclean. The same week of waiting is used for cloth (verse 50) and for a house (14:38). The law gives no reason of health; the waiting is so that the ruling will be right.

decisions.choice: the one with the mark: the person who has it
decisions.reason: The word 'mark' here stands for the person who bears it, as in verses 12, 13, 17 and 31.

decisions.choice: shut away / keep away from others
decisions.reason: Literal keeps 'shut up'. Balanced says 'shut away', and Readable says what that means for the person. 'Quarantine' is avoided, since the law does not give health as its reason.

decisions.choice: "encerrar" (L); "aislar" (B); "mantener apartada de los demás" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the plain verb "shut up"; Balanced and Readable say what it means for the person. "Cuarentena" is avoided, as the English avoids "quarantine", since the law gives no reason of health. The same words are used for every week of waiting in chapters 13 and 14.

decisions.choice: "enfermer" (L); "isoler" (B); "tenir à l'écart des autres" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the plain verb "shut up"; Balanced and Readable say what it means for the person. "Quarantaine" is avoided, as the English avoids "quarantine", since the law gives no reason of health. The same words are used for every week of waiting in chapters 13 and 14.

decisions.choice: "kumfungia" (L); "kumtenga" (B); "kumweka mbali na watu wengine" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the plain verb "shut up"; Balanced and Readable say what it means for the person. "Karantini" is avoided, as the English avoids "quarantine", since the law gives no reason of health. The same words are used for every week of waiting in chapters 13 and 14.

source.text: וְרָאָ֣הוּ הַכֹּהֵן֮ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי֒ וְהִנֵּ֤ה הַנֶּ֨גַע֙ עָמַ֣ד בְּעֵינָ֔יו לֹֽא־פָשָׂ֥ה הַנֶּ֖גַע בָּע֑וֹר וְהִסְגִּיר֧וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֛ן שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים שֵׁנִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And will see him the priest on the seventh day, and there! the mark has stood in his eyes, not has spread the mark in the skin, then will shut him up the priest seven days [a] second [time].

en.L: And the priest shall look at him on the seventh day, and there! the mark has stood in his eyes; the mark has not spread in the skin; then the priest shall shut him up seven days a second [time].
en.B: On the seventh day the priest is to look at the person again. If in his judgment the sore is unchanged and has not spread in the skin, he is to shut them away for another seven days.
en.R: On the seventh day the priest must look again. If he sees that the sore has not changed or spread, he must keep the person away from others for seven more days.

es.L: Y el sacerdote lo mirará el séptimo día, y he aquí, la marca se ha mantenido a sus ojos; no se ha extendido la marca en la piel; entonces el sacerdote lo encerrará siete días por segunda [vez].
es.B: El séptimo día el sacerdote volverá a examinar a la persona. Si a su juicio la llaga sigue igual y no se ha extendido por la piel, la aislará otros siete días.
es.R: El séptimo día el sacerdote tiene que mirar otra vez. Si ve que la llaga no ha cambiado ni se ha extendido, tiene que mantener a la persona apartada de los demás siete días más.

fr.L: Et le prêtre le regardera le septième jour, et voici, la marque s’est maintenue à ses yeux ; la marque ne s’est pas étendue sur la peau ; alors le prêtre l’enfermera sept jours une seconde [fois].
fr.B: Le septième jour, le prêtre examinera de nouveau la personne. Si, à son avis, la lésion n’a pas changé et ne s’est pas étendue sur la peau, il l’isolera encore sept jours.
fr.R: Le septième jour, le prêtre doit regarder encore. S’il voit que la plaie n’a pas changé et ne s’est pas étendue, il doit tenir la personne à l’écart des autres pendant sept jours de plus.

sw.L: Na kuhani atamwangalia siku ya saba, na tazama, alama imesimama machoni pake; alama haijaenea katika ngozi; ndipo kuhani atamfungia siku saba mara ya pili.
sw.B: Siku ya saba kuhani atamwangalia mtu huyo tena. Ikiwa kwa maoni yake kidonda hakijabadilika wala hakijaenea katika ngozi, atamtenga kwa siku nyingine saba.
sw.R: Siku ya saba lazima kuhani aangalie tena. Akiona kwamba kidonda hakijabadilika wala hakijaenea, lazima amweke mtu huyo mbali na watu wengine kwa siku saba zaidi.

decisions.choice: has stood in his eyes: as far as the priest can see, it has not changed
decisions.reason: 'In his eyes' means in the priest's sight or judgment. The mark has 'stood', that is, stayed as it was (compare verses 23, 28 and 37).

decisions.choice: spread: grown wider over the skin
decisions.reason: Spreading is the main sign of an active disease in skin, cloth and house (verses 7-8, 22, 27, 51; 14:39).

source.text: וְרָאָה֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן אֹת֜וֹ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי֮ שֵׁנִית֒ וְהִנֵּה֙ כֵּהָ֣ה הַנֶּ֔גַע וְלֹא־פָשָׂ֥ה הַנֶּ֖גַע בָּע֑וֹר וְטִהֲר֤וֹ הַכֹּהֵן֙ מִסְפַּ֣חַת הִ֔יא וְכִבֶּ֥ס בְּגָדָ֖יו וְטָהֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And will see the priest him on the seventh day [a] second [time], and there! has grown faint the mark, and has not spread the mark in the skin, then will pronounce him clean the priest; [a] scab it [is]; and he will wash his garments and be clean.

en.L: And the priest shall look at him on the seventh day a second [time], and there! the mark has grown faint, and the mark has not spread in the skin; then the priest shall pronounce him clean; it [is] a scab; and he shall wash his garments and be clean.
en.B: When the second seven days are over, the priest is to look once more. If the sore has grown dim and not spread over the skin, it is merely a scab, and the priest is to declare the person clean. After washing their clothes, they are clean.
en.R: At the end of the second seven days, the priest must look at it again. The sore may have become pale without spreading. Then the priest must say that the person is clean. It is only a scab. The person must wash their clothes. Then they will be clean.

es.L: Y el sacerdote lo mirará el séptimo día por segunda [vez], y he aquí, la marca se ha apagado, y no se ha extendido la marca en la piel; entonces el sacerdote lo declarará puro; costra [es]; y lavará sus vestidos y será puro.
es.B: Al cumplirse los otros siete días, el sacerdote volverá a examinarla. Si la llaga ha perdido color y no se ha extendido por la piel, no es más que una costra, y el sacerdote declarará pura a la persona. Después de lavar su ropa, quedará pura.
es.R: Al final de los otros siete días, el sacerdote tiene que mirarla otra vez. Puede que la llaga se haya puesto pálida sin extenderse. Entonces el sacerdote tiene que decir que la persona es pura. Es solo una costra. La persona tiene que lavar su ropa. Después quedará pura.

fr.L: Et le prêtre le regardera le septième jour une seconde [fois], et voici, la marque est devenue terne, et la marque ne s’est pas étendue sur la peau ; alors le prêtre le déclarera pur ; c’[est] une croûte ; et il lavera ses vêtements et sera pur.
fr.B: Au terme des sept jours suivants, le prêtre examinera de nouveau la personne. Si la lésion a pâli et ne s’est pas étendue sur la peau, ce n’est qu’une croûte, et le prêtre la déclarera pure. Après avoir lavé ses vêtements, elle sera pure.
fr.R: À la fin des sept autres jours, le prêtre doit regarder la plaie encore une fois. Elle est peut-être devenue pâle sans s’étendre. Alors le prêtre doit dire que la personne est pure. Ce n’est qu’une croûte. La personne doit laver ses vêtements. Ensuite, elle sera pure.

sw.L: Na kuhani atamwangalia siku ya saba mara ya pili, na tazama, alama imefifia, na alama haijaenea katika ngozi; ndipo kuhani atamtangaza kuwa safi; ni kigaga; naye atafua nguo zake na kuwa safi.
sw.B: Siku saba za pili zikiisha, kuhani atamwangalia tena. Ikiwa kidonda kimefifia na hakijaenea katika ngozi, ni kigaga tu, na kuhani atamtangaza mtu huyo kuwa safi. Akishafua nguo zake, atakuwa safi.
sw.R: Mwishoni mwa siku saba za pili, lazima kuhani aangalie tena. Huenda kidonda kimepauka bila kuenea. Basi lazima kuhani aseme kwamba mtu huyo ni safi. Ni kigaga tu. Lazima mtu huyo afue nguo zake. Kisha atakuwa safi.

decisions.choice: grown faint: the mark has become dim or pale
decisions.reason: The verb means to grow dim or faint, as weak eyes do (Genesis 27:1). A fading mark is a sign that it is not the disease; the same word comes in verses 21, 26, 28, 39 and 56.

decisions.choice: a scab: a harmless crusting of the skin
decisions.reason: The word is related to 'scab' in verse 2. Here it names flaking or crusting that is not the disease. If it later spreads, the ruling changes (verses 7-8).

decisions.choice: wash his garments and be clean: a washing at the end of the time of doubt
decisions.reason: The person was never declared unclean, yet washes before taking up ordinary life again, as in verse 34.

decisions.choice: the second seven days
decisions.reason: 'On the seventh day a second time' means at the end of the second week (verse 5). Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: וְאִם־פָּשֹׂ֨ה תִפְשֶׂ֤ה הַמִּסְפַּ֨חַת֙ בָּע֔וֹר אַחֲרֵ֧י הֵרָאֹת֛וֹ אֶל־הַכֹּהֵ֖ן לְטָהֳרָת֑וֹ וְנִרְאָ֥ה שֵׁנִ֖ית אֶל־הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And if indeed will spread the scab in the skin after he has shown himself to the priest for his cleansing, and he will show himself [a] second [time] to the priest.

en.L: But if the scab indeed spreads in the skin after he has shown himself to the priest for his cleansing, then he shall show himself to the priest a second [time].
en.B: But if the scab spreads in the skin after they have shown themselves to the priest and been declared clean, they must come before the priest again.
en.R: But the scab may spread on the skin after the priest has said that the person is clean. Then the person must go back to the priest.

es.L: Pero si la costra en verdad se extiende en la piel después de haberse mostrado al sacerdote para su purificación, se mostrará por segunda [vez] al sacerdote.
es.B: Pero si la costra se extiende por la piel después de que la persona se ha presentado al sacerdote y ha sido declarada pura, tendrá que presentarse de nuevo ante el sacerdote.
es.R: Pero puede que la costra se extienda por la piel después de que el sacerdote haya dicho que la persona es pura. Entonces la persona tiene que volver al sacerdote.

fr.L: Mais si la croûte s’étend vraiment sur la peau après qu’il s’est montré au prêtre pour sa purification, il se montrera une seconde [fois] au prêtre.
fr.B: Mais si la croûte s’étend sur la peau après que la personne s’est montrée au prêtre et a été déclarée pure, elle devra se présenter de nouveau devant le prêtre.
fr.R: Mais il arrive que la croûte s’étende sur la peau après que le prêtre a dit que la personne était pure. Alors la personne doit retourner voir le prêtre.

sw.L: Lakini kigaga kikienea kweli katika ngozi baada ya yeye kujionyesha kwa kuhani kwa ajili ya kutakaswa kwake, atajionyesha kwa kuhani mara ya pili.
sw.B: Lakini kigaga kikienea katika ngozi baada ya mtu huyo kujionyesha kwa kuhani na kutangazwa kuwa safi, atakwenda tena kwa kuhani.
sw.R: Lakini huenda kigaga kikaenea kwenye ngozi baada ya kuhani kusema kwamba mtu huyo ni safi. Basi lazima mtu huyo arudi kwa kuhani.

decisions.choice: indeed spreads: if it really does spread
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis, as again in verses 22, 27 and 35.

decisions.choice: shown himself for his cleansing: been seen by the priest and declared clean
decisions.reason: 'For his cleansing' refers to the ruling of verse 6. The case can be opened again if the mark later spreads.

decisions.choice: and been declared clean / after the priest has said that the person is clean
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out what 'for his cleansing' refers to (verse 6).

source.text: וְרָאָה֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהִנֵּ֛ה פָּשְׂתָ֥ה הַמִּסְפַּ֖חַת בָּע֑וֹר וְטִמְּא֥וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן צָרַ֥עַת הִֽוא׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And will see the priest, and there! has spread the scab in the skin, then will pronounce him unclean the priest; scale disease it [is].

en.L: And the priest shall look, and there! the scab has spread in the skin; then the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it [is] scale disease.
en.B: If the priest sees that the scab has spread in the skin, he is to declare the person unclean: it is a serious skin disease.
en.R: The priest must look again. If the scab has spread, he must say that the person is unclean. It is a serious skin disease.

es.L: Y el sacerdote mirará, y he aquí, la costra se ha extendido en la piel; entonces el sacerdote lo declarará impuro; enfermedad de la piel [es].
es.B: Si el sacerdote ve que la costra se ha extendido por la piel, declarará impura a la persona: es una enfermedad grave de la piel.
es.R: El sacerdote tiene que mirar otra vez. Si la costra se ha extendido, tiene que decir que la persona es impura. Es una enfermedad grave de la piel.

fr.L: Et le prêtre regardera, et voici, la croûte s’est étendue sur la peau ; alors le prêtre le déclarera impur ; c’[est] une maladie de peau.
fr.B: Si le prêtre constate que la croûte s’est étendue sur la peau, il déclarera la personne impure : c’est une maladie de peau grave.
fr.R: Le prêtre doit regarder encore. Si la croûte s’est étendue, il doit dire que la personne est impure. C’est une maladie de peau grave.

sw.L: Na kuhani ataangalia, na tazama, kigaga kimeenea katika ngozi; ndipo kuhani atamtangaza kuwa najisi; ni ugonjwa wa ngozi.
sw.B: Kuhani akiona kwamba kigaga kimeenea katika ngozi, atamtangaza mtu huyo kuwa najisi: ni ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi.
sw.R: Lazima kuhani aangalie tena. Ikiwa kigaga kimeenea, lazima aseme kwamba mtu huyo ni najisi. Ni ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi.

decisions.choice: it is scale disease: the spreading settles the case
decisions.reason: What was thought to be a harmless scab is now ruled to be the disease itself. Spreading is the deciding sign (verse 5).

source.text: נֶ֣גַע צָרַ֔עַת כִּ֥י תִהְיֶ֖ה בְּאָדָ֑ם וְהוּבָ֖א אֶל־הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] mark of scale disease, when it will be on [a] person, then he will be brought to the priest.

en.L: When a mark of scale disease is on a person, then he shall be brought to the priest.
en.B: Anyone who has a sore of serious skin disease is to be brought to the priest.
en.R: When a person has a sore from a serious skin disease, they must be taken to the priest.

es.L: Cuando haya marca de enfermedad de la piel en una persona, será llevada al sacerdote.
es.B: Toda persona que tenga una llaga de enfermedad grave de la piel será llevada al sacerdote.
es.R: Cuando alguien tiene una llaga por una enfermedad grave de la piel, hay que llevarlo al sacerdote.

fr.L: Lorsqu’une marque de maladie de peau sera sur quelqu’un, il sera amené au prêtre.
fr.B: Toute personne qui porte une lésion de maladie de peau grave sera amenée au prêtre.
fr.R: Quand une personne a la plaie d’une maladie de peau grave, il faut l’amener au prêtre.

sw.L: Alama ya ugonjwa wa ngozi itakapokuwa juu ya mtu, ataletwa kwa kuhani.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote mwenye kidonda cha ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi ataletwa kwa kuhani.
sw.R: Mtu akiwa na kidonda cha ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi, lazima apelekwe kwa kuhani.

decisions.choice: a second case: a mark already there, not only a first sign
decisions.reason: Verses 2-8 began with a first sign that might become the disease. Verses 9-17 deal with a mark already on a person. The word for 'person' is again the general word for a human being (verse 2).

source.text: וְרָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה שְׂאֵת־לְבָנָה֙ בָּע֔וֹר וְהִ֕יא הָפְכָ֖ה שֵׂעָ֣ר לָבָ֑ן וּמִֽחְיַ֛ת בָּשָׂ֥ר חַ֖י בַּשְׂאֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And will see the priest, and there! [a] swelling white [is] in the skin, and it has turned [the] hair white, and [a] raw spot of living flesh [is] in the swelling,

en.L: And the priest shall look, and there! [there is] a white swelling in the skin, and it has turned the hair white, and [there is] a raw spot of living flesh in the swelling,
en.B: The priest is to look. If there is a white swelling in the skin that has turned the hair white, and there is raw flesh in the swelling,
en.R: The priest must look at the skin. He may see a white swelling that has turned the hair white, with raw flesh in it.

es.L: Y el sacerdote mirará, y he aquí, [hay] una hinchazón blanca en la piel, y ha vuelto blanco el pelo, y [hay] un punto de carne viva en la hinchazón,
es.B: El sacerdote la examinará. Si hay en la piel una hinchazón blanca que ha vuelto blanco el pelo, y hay carne viva en la hinchazón,
es.R: El sacerdote tiene que mirar la piel. Puede que vea una hinchazón blanca que ha vuelto blanco el pelo, con carne viva en ella.

fr.L: Et le prêtre regardera, et voici, [il y a] une enflure blanche sur la peau, et elle a fait blanchir le poil, et [il y a] une trace de chair vive dans l’enflure,
fr.B: Le prêtre examinera la personne. S’il y a sur la peau une enflure blanche qui a fait blanchir le poil, et de la chair vive dans l’enflure,
fr.R: Le prêtre doit regarder la peau. Il voit peut-être une enflure blanche qui a fait blanchir les poils, avec de la chair vive dedans.

sw.L: Na kuhani ataangalia, na tazama, [kuna] uvimbe mweupe katika ngozi, nao umegeuza nywele kuwa nyeupe, na [kuna] sehemu ya nyama hai katika uvimbe,
sw.B: Kuhani ataangalia. Ikiwa kuna uvimbe mweupe katika ngozi ambao umegeuza nywele kuwa nyeupe, na kuna nyama mbichi katika uvimbe huo,
sw.R: Lazima kuhani aiangalie ngozi. Huenda akaona uvimbe mweupe ambao umefanya nywele kuwa nyeupe, wenye nyama mbichi ndani yake.

decisions.choice: a raw spot of living flesh: raw, open flesh showing in the swelling
decisions.reason: 'Living flesh' is flesh that looks raw, not covered by healthy skin; the first word means something like a quickening or a patch of raw flesh. It is the sign of active disease again in verses 14-16, and in verse 24 it names the raw place of a burn.

decisions.choice: it has turned the hair white: the swelling has changed the hair growing in it
decisions.reason: The swelling is the subject; compare verse 3.

decisions.choice: raw flesh
decisions.reason: Literal keeps 'living flesh', as the Hebrew has it. Balanced and Readable say 'raw flesh', which is what is meant, here and in verses 14-16.

decisions.choice: "carne viva" at every level
decisions.reason: Spanish "carne viva" says word for word what the Hebrew says, "living flesh", and is also the ordinary Spanish for raw, open flesh, so one phrase serves all three levels here and in verses 14-16 and 24.

decisions.choice: "chair vive" at every level
decisions.reason: French "chair vive" says word for word what the Hebrew says, "living flesh", and is also the ordinary French for raw, open flesh, so one phrase serves all three levels here and in verses 14-16 and 24.

decisions.choice: "nyama hai" (L); "nyama mbichi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "nyama hai", living flesh, as the Hebrew has it; Balanced and Readable say "nyama mbichi", raw flesh, as the English says "raw flesh".

source.text: צָרַ֨עַת נוֹשֶׁ֤נֶת הִוא֙ בְּע֣וֹר בְּשָׂר֔וֹ וְטִמְּא֖וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֑ן לֹ֣א יַסְגִּרֶ֔נּוּ כִּ֥י טָמֵ֖א הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: [an] old scale disease it [is] in [the] skin of his flesh, and will pronounce him unclean the priest; not will he shut him up, for unclean he [is].

en.L: it [is] an old scale disease in the skin of his flesh, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean; he shall not shut him up, for he [is] unclean.
en.B: it is a long-standing serious skin disease in the skin of the body. The priest is to declare the person unclean without shutting them away, for there is no doubt that they are unclean.
en.R: Then the person has had a serious skin disease for a long time. The priest must say that they are unclean. He does not need to keep them away for seven days to find out, because it is clear that they are unclean.

es.L: una enfermedad de la piel antigua [es] en la piel de su carne, y el sacerdote lo declarará impuro; no lo encerrará, porque impuro [es].
es.B: es una enfermedad grave de la piel arraigada desde hace tiempo en la piel del cuerpo. El sacerdote declarará impura a la persona sin aislarla, porque no hay duda de que es impura.
es.R: Entonces la persona tiene desde hace mucho tiempo una enfermedad grave de la piel. El sacerdote tiene que decir que es impura. No necesita mantenerla apartada siete días para averiguarlo, porque está claro que es impura.

fr.L: c’[est] une maladie de peau ancienne dans la peau de sa chair, et le prêtre le déclarera impur ; il ne l’enfermera pas, car il [est] impur.
fr.B: c’est une maladie de peau grave installée depuis longtemps dans la peau du corps. Le prêtre déclarera la personne impure sans l’isoler, car il n’y a aucun doute qu’elle est impure.
fr.R: Alors la personne a une maladie de peau grave depuis longtemps. Le prêtre doit dire qu’elle est impure. Il n’a pas besoin de la tenir à l’écart sept jours pour le savoir, car il est clair qu’elle est impure.

sw.L: ni ugonjwa wa ngozi wa zamani katika ngozi ya mwili wake, na kuhani atamtangaza kuwa najisi; hatamfungia, kwa maana yeye [ni] najisi.
sw.B: ni ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi uliokaa muda mrefu katika ngozi ya mwili. Kuhani atamtangaza mtu huyo kuwa najisi bila kumtenga, kwa maana hakuna shaka kwamba yeye ni najisi.
sw.R: Basi mtu huyo amekuwa na ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi kwa muda mrefu. Lazima kuhani aseme kwamba yeye ni najisi. Hahitaji kumweka mbali na watu kwa siku saba ili kujua, kwa sababu ni wazi kwamba yeye ni najisi.

decisions.choice: old: long-standing, well established
decisions.reason: The word means grown old. The raw flesh and white hair show that the disease has been there for some time.

decisions.choice: he shall not shut him up: no week of waiting is needed
decisions.reason: The waiting of verses 4-5 is for doubtful cases. Here the signs are clear.

decisions.choice: there is no doubt / it is clear
decisions.reason: 'For he is unclean' gives the reason no waiting is needed. Balanced and Readable say it in those terms; Readable also names the seven days of verse 4.

source.text: וְאִם־פָּר֨וֹחַ תִּפְרַ֤ח הַצָּרַ֨עַת֙ בָּע֔וֹר וְכִסְּתָ֣ה הַצָּרַ֗עַת אֵ֚ת כָּל־ע֣וֹר הַנֶּ֔גַע מֵרֹאשׁ֖וֹ וְעַד־רַגְלָ֑יו לְכָל־מַרְאֵ֖ה עֵינֵ֥י הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And if indeed will break out the scale disease in the skin, and will cover the scale disease all [the] skin of the [one with the] mark from his head and to his feet, to all [the] sight of [the] eyes of the priest,

en.L: And if the scale disease indeed breaks out in the skin, and the scale disease covers all the skin of the [one with the] mark from his head to his feet, to all the sight of the eyes of the priest,
en.B: If the disease breaks out all over the skin and covers the whole skin of the person with the sore, from head to foot, wherever the priest looks,
en.R: Sometimes the skin disease spreads until it covers the person's whole body from head to foot. The priest sees it everywhere he looks.

es.L: Y si en verdad brota la enfermedad de la piel en la piel, y cubre la enfermedad de la piel toda la piel [del que tiene] la marca, desde su cabeza hasta sus pies, a toda la vista de los ojos del sacerdote,
es.B: Si la enfermedad brota por toda la piel y cubre toda la piel de la persona que tiene la llaga, de la cabeza a los pies, dondequiera que mire el sacerdote,
es.R: A veces la enfermedad de la piel se extiende hasta cubrir todo el cuerpo de la persona, de la cabeza a los pies. El sacerdote la ve en cualquier parte donde mira.

fr.L: Et si la maladie de peau éclate vraiment sur la peau, et [si] la maladie de peau couvre toute la peau [de celui qui a] la marque, de sa tête jusqu’à ses pieds, à toute la vue des yeux du prêtre,
fr.B: Si la maladie se répand sur toute la peau et couvre entièrement la peau de la personne atteinte, de la tête aux pieds, partout où le prêtre regarde,
fr.R: Parfois la maladie de peau s’étend jusqu’à couvrir tout le corps de la personne, de la tête aux pieds. Le prêtre la voit partout où il regarde.

sw.L: Na ikiwa ugonjwa wa ngozi utachipuka kweli katika ngozi, na ugonjwa wa ngozi ukafunika ngozi yote ya [mwenye] alama kutoka kichwa chake hadi miguu yake, kwa kadiri yote ya kuona kwa macho ya kuhani,
sw.B: Ugonjwa ukienea katika ngozi yote na kufunika ngozi nzima ya mtu mwenye kidonda, kutoka kichwani hadi miguuni, kila mahali kuhani anapoangalia,
sw.R: Wakati mwingine ugonjwa wa ngozi huenea mpaka kufunika mwili mzima wa mtu, kutoka kichwani hadi miguuni. Kuhani anauona kila mahali anapoangalia.

decisions.choice: breaks out: blossoms over the skin
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a plant that buds or blossoms (Numbers 17:8). Here the disease spreads over the skin as a plant breaks into flower; the doubled verb stresses it.

decisions.choice: to all the sight of the priest's eyes: everywhere the priest looks
decisions.reason: The phrase means that the priest can find no part of the skin it has not reached.

source.text: וְרָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֨ה כִסְּתָ֤ה הַצָּרַ֨עַת֙ אֶת־כָּל־בְּשָׂר֔וֹ וְטִהַ֖ר אֶת־הַנָּ֑גַע כֻּלּ֛וֹ הָפַ֥ךְ לָבָ֖ן טָה֥וֹר הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: and will see the priest, and there! has covered the scale disease all his flesh, then he will pronounce clean the [one with the] mark; all of it has turned white; clean he [is].

en.L: and the priest shall look, and there! the scale disease has covered all his flesh, then he shall pronounce the [one with the] mark clean; all of it has turned white; he [is] clean.
en.B: the priest is to look, and if the disease has covered the whole body, he is to declare the person clean. It has all turned white; they are clean.
en.R: If the priest sees that the disease covers the whole body and has all turned white, he must say that the person is clean. They are clean.

es.L: y el sacerdote mirará, y he aquí, la enfermedad de la piel ha cubierto toda su carne; entonces declarará puro [al que tiene] la marca; todo se ha vuelto blanco; puro [es].
es.B: el sacerdote la examinará, y si la enfermedad ha cubierto todo el cuerpo, declarará pura a la persona. Todo se ha vuelto blanco; es pura.
es.R: Si el sacerdote ve que la enfermedad cubre todo el cuerpo y que todo se ha vuelto blanco, tiene que decir que la persona es pura. Es pura.

fr.L: et le prêtre regardera, et voici, la maladie de peau a couvert toute sa chair ; alors il déclarera pur [celui qui a] la marque ; tout est devenu blanc ; il [est] pur.
fr.B: le prêtre l’examinera, et si la maladie a couvert tout le corps, il déclarera la personne pure. Tout est devenu blanc : elle est pure.
fr.R: Si le prêtre voit que la maladie couvre tout le corps et que tout est devenu blanc, il doit dire que la personne est pure. Elle est pure.

sw.L: na kuhani ataangalia, na tazama, ugonjwa wa ngozi umefunika mwili wake wote; ndipo atamtangaza [mwenye] alama kuwa safi; wote umegeuka kuwa mweupe; yeye [ni] safi.
sw.B: kuhani ataangalia, na ikiwa ugonjwa umefunika mwili wote, atamtangaza mtu huyo kuwa safi. Mwili wote umekuwa mweupe; yeye ni safi.
sw.R: Kuhani akiona kwamba ugonjwa unafunika mwili wote na wote umekuwa mweupe, lazima aseme kwamba mtu huyo ni safi. Yeye ni safi.

decisions.choice: all of it has turned white; he is clean: skin wholly white is not unclean
decisions.reason: This is the surprising case of the chapter. When the whole skin has turned white and no raw flesh shows (verse 14), the person is clean. The text does not say why. It may be that the disease has run its course and the skin has healed over white; in these laws uncleanness goes with what is raw, open or spreading.

decisions.choice: the person
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says 'the one with the mark'; Balanced and Readable say 'the person', as in verse 4.

source.text: וּבְי֨וֹם הֵרָא֥וֹת בּ֛וֹ בָּשָׂ֥ר חַ֖י יִטְמָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And on [the] day [that] appears in him living flesh, he will be unclean.

en.L: But on the day [that] living flesh appears in him, he shall be unclean.
en.B: But whenever raw flesh appears on them, they will be unclean.
en.R: But if raw flesh ever shows up on them, they will be unclean.

es.L: Pero el día [en que] aparezca en él carne viva, será impuro.
es.B: Pero cuando aparezca en ella carne viva, será impura.
es.R: Pero si alguna vez le aparece carne viva, será impura.

fr.L: Mais le jour [où] apparaîtra en lui de la chair vive, il sera impur.
fr.B: Mais dès que de la chair vive apparaîtra sur elle, elle sera impure.
fr.R: Mais si un jour de la chair vive se montre sur elle, elle sera impure.

sw.L: Lakini siku [ambayo] nyama hai itaonekana kwake, atakuwa najisi.
sw.B: Lakini wakati wowote nyama mbichi itakapoonekana kwake, atakuwa najisi.
sw.R: Lakini nyama mbichi ikitokea kwake wakati wowote, atakuwa najisi.

decisions.choice: on the day: whenever, as soon as
decisions.reason: 'On the day' means 'when'. The ruling of verse 13 holds only while no raw flesh shows.

source.text: וְרָאָ֧ה הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֶת־הַבָּשָׂ֥ר הַחַ֖י וְטִמְּא֑וֹ הַבָּשָׂ֥ר הַחַ֛י טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא צָרַ֥עַת הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And will see the priest the living flesh and will pronounce him unclean; the living flesh unclean it [is]; scale disease it [is].

en.L: And the priest shall look at the living flesh and pronounce him unclean; the living flesh, it [is] unclean; it [is] scale disease.
en.B: The priest is to look at the raw flesh and declare the person unclean. Raw flesh is unclean; it is a serious skin disease.
en.R: The priest must look at the raw flesh and say that the person is unclean. Raw flesh is unclean. It shows a serious skin disease.

es.L: Y el sacerdote mirará la carne viva y lo declarará impuro; la carne viva, impura [es]; enfermedad de la piel [es].
es.B: El sacerdote mirará la carne viva y declarará impura a la persona. La carne viva es impura; es una enfermedad grave de la piel.
es.R: El sacerdote tiene que mirar la carne viva y decir que la persona es impura. La carne viva es impura. Muestra una enfermedad grave de la piel.

fr.L: Et le prêtre regardera la chair vive et le déclarera impur ; la chair vive, elle [est] impure ; c’[est] une maladie de peau.
fr.B: Le prêtre examinera la chair vive et déclarera la personne impure. La chair vive est impure : c’est une maladie de peau grave.
fr.R: Le prêtre doit regarder la chair vive et dire que la personne est impure. La chair vive est impure. Elle montre une maladie de peau grave.

sw.L: Na kuhani ataiangalia nyama hai na kumtangaza kuwa najisi; nyama hai ni najisi; ni ugonjwa wa ngozi.
sw.B: Kuhani ataiangalia nyama mbichi na kumtangaza mtu huyo kuwa najisi. Nyama mbichi ni najisi; ni ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi.
sw.R: Lazima kuhani aiangalie nyama mbichi na kusema kwamba mtu huyo ni najisi. Nyama mbichi ni najisi. Inaonyesha ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi.

decisions.choice: the living flesh is unclean: raw flesh is the sign of active disease
decisions.reason: The raw flesh itself is what makes the case unclean, as in verse 10.

source.text: א֣וֹ כִ֥י יָשׁ֛וּב הַבָּשָׂ֥ר הַחַ֖י וְנֶהְפַּ֣ךְ לְלָבָ֑ן וּבָ֖א אֶל־הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: Or when will turn back the living flesh and be changed to white, then he will come to the priest.

en.L: Or if the living flesh turns back and is changed to white, then he shall come to the priest.
en.B: But if the raw flesh changes again and turns white, they are to go to the priest.
en.R: But the raw flesh may change and turn white. Then the person must go to the priest.

es.L: O si la carne viva vuelve y se torna blanca, vendrá al sacerdote.
es.B: Pero si la carne viva cambia de nuevo y se vuelve blanca, la persona irá al sacerdote.
es.R: Pero puede que la carne viva cambie y se vuelva blanca. Entonces la persona tiene que ir al sacerdote.

fr.L: Ou si la chair vive revient et se change en blanc, il viendra au prêtre.
fr.B: Mais si la chair vive change de nouveau et devient blanche, la personne ira trouver le prêtre.
fr.R: Mais la chair vive peut changer et devenir blanche. Alors la personne doit aller voir le prêtre.

sw.L: Au nyama hai ikirudi na kugeuzwa kuwa nyeupe, atakuja kwa kuhani.
sw.B: Lakini nyama mbichi ikibadilika tena na kuwa nyeupe, mtu huyo atakwenda kwa kuhani.
sw.R: Lakini huenda nyama mbichi ikabadilika na kuwa nyeupe. Basi lazima mtu huyo aende kwa kuhani.

decisions.choice: turns back: changes again
decisions.reason: 'Return' with another verb can mean 'again'. The raw flesh heals over and the skin turns white, as in verse 13.

source.text: וְרָאָ֨הוּ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהִנֵּ֛ה נֶהְפַּ֥ךְ הַנֶּ֖גַע לְלָבָ֑ן וְטִהַ֧ר הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֶת־הַנֶּ֖גַע טָה֥וֹר הֽוּא׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And will see him the priest, and there! has been changed the mark to white, then will pronounce clean the priest the [one with the] mark; clean he [is].

en.L: And the priest shall look at him, and there! the mark has been changed to white; then the priest shall pronounce the [one with the] mark clean; he [is] clean.
en.B: The priest is to examine them, and if the sore has turned white, he is to declare the person with the sore clean. They are clean.
en.R: The priest must look at the person. If the sore has turned white, he must say that the person is clean. They are clean.

es.L: Y el sacerdote lo mirará, y he aquí, la marca se ha cambiado en blanco; entonces el sacerdote declarará puro [al que tiene] la marca; puro [es].
es.B: El sacerdote la examinará, y si la llaga se ha vuelto blanca, declarará pura a la persona que tiene la llaga. Es pura.
es.R: El sacerdote tiene que mirar a la persona. Si la llaga se ha vuelto blanca, tiene que decir que la persona es pura. Es pura.

fr.L: Et le prêtre le regardera, et voici, la marque s’est changée en blanc ; alors le prêtre déclarera pur [celui qui a] la marque ; il [est] pur.
fr.B: Le prêtre l’examinera, et si la lésion est devenue blanche, il déclarera pure la personne atteinte. Elle est pure.
fr.R: Le prêtre doit regarder la personne. Si la plaie est devenue blanche, il doit dire que la personne est pure. Elle est pure.

sw.L: Na kuhani atamwangalia, na tazama, alama imegeuzwa kuwa nyeupe; ndipo kuhani atamtangaza [mwenye] alama kuwa safi; yeye [ni] safi.
sw.B: Kuhani atamchunguza, na ikiwa kidonda kimekuwa cheupe, atamtangaza mtu mwenye kidonda kuwa safi. Yeye ni safi.
sw.R: Lazima kuhani amwangalie mtu huyo. Ikiwa kidonda kimekuwa cheupe, lazima aseme kwamba mtu huyo ni safi. Yeye ni safi.

decisions.choice: he is clean: the closing words of the ruling
decisions.reason: Each case ends with a short verdict, 'he is clean' or 'he is unclean' (verses 11, 13, 15), probably the words the priest spoke.

source.text: וּבָשָׂ֕ר כִּֽי־יִהְיֶ֥ה בֽוֹ־בְעֹר֖וֹ שְׁחִ֑ין וְנִרְפָּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And flesh, when will be in it, in its skin, [a] boil, and it is healed,

en.L: And [as for] flesh, when there is in it, in its skin, a boil, and it is healed,
en.B: When someone has a boil on their skin and it has healed,
en.R: Someone may have a boil on their skin that heals.

es.L: Y [en cuanto a] la carne, cuando haya en ella, en su piel, un forúnculo, y se haya curado,
es.B: Cuando alguien tenga en la piel un forúnculo y este se haya curado,
es.R: Puede que alguien tenga en la piel un forúnculo que se cura.

fr.L: Et [quant à] la chair, lorsqu’il y aura en elle, dans sa peau, un furoncle, et qu’il aura guéri,
fr.B: Lorsque quelqu’un a eu un furoncle sur la peau et qu’il a guéri,
fr.R: Il peut arriver qu’une personne ait sur la peau un furoncle qui guérit.

sw.L: Na [kuhusu] mwili, utakapokuwa na jipu ndani yake, katika ngozi yake, nalo likapona,
sw.B: Mtu akiwa na jipu kwenye ngozi yake, nalo likapona,
sw.R: Huenda mtu akawa na jipu kwenye ngozi yake, nalo likapona.

decisions.choice: boil: an inflamed swelling or sore on the skin
decisions.reason: The word is used for the boils of the sixth plague in Egypt (Exodus 9:9-11), for Hezekiah's illness (2 Kings 20:7) and for the sores of Job (Job 2:7). Here the boil itself has healed; the question is what appears in its place (verse 19).

decisions.choice: flesh: a body, a person
decisions.reason: 'Flesh' stands for a person's body. As in verse 2, the case is for men and women alike.

source.text: וְהָיָ֞ה בִּמְק֤וֹם הַשְּׁחִין֙ שְׂאֵ֣ת לְבָנָ֔ה א֥וֹ בַהֶ֖רֶת לְבָנָ֣ה אֲדַמְדָּ֑מֶת וְנִרְאָ֖ה אֶל־הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: and is in [the] place of the boil [a] swelling white or [a] bright spot white reddish, then he will show himself to the priest.

en.L: and there is in the place of the boil a white swelling or a reddish-white bright spot, then he shall show himself to the priest.
en.B: and a white swelling or a reddish-white bright spot appears where the boil was, they are to show it to the priest.
en.R: Later a white swelling or a pinkish-white shiny spot may appear where the boil was. Then the person must show it to the priest.

es.L: y haya en el lugar del forúnculo una hinchazón blanca o una mancha brillante blanca rojiza, se mostrará al sacerdote.
es.B: y en el lugar del forúnculo aparece una hinchazón blanca o una mancha brillante de color blanco rojizo, la persona se la mostrará al sacerdote.
es.R: Más tarde, donde estaba el forúnculo, puede aparecer una hinchazón blanca o una mancha que brilla de color blanco rosado. Entonces la persona tiene que mostrársela al sacerdote.

fr.L: et qu’il y aura à la place du furoncle une enflure blanche ou une tache brillante d’un blanc rougeâtre, il se montrera au prêtre.
fr.B: et qu’une enflure blanche ou une tache brillante d’un blanc rougeâtre apparaît là où était le furoncle, la personne la montrera au prêtre.
fr.R: Plus tard, une enflure blanche ou une tache qui brille, d’un blanc rosé, peut apparaître là où était le furoncle. Alors la personne doit la montrer au prêtre.

sw.L: na pakawa mahali pa jipu uvimbe mweupe au doa linalong'aa jeupe lenye wekundu, atajionyesha kwa kuhani.
sw.B: na mahali lilipokuwa jipu ukatokea uvimbe mweupe au doa linalong'aa jeupe lenye wekundu, mtu huyo atamwonyesha kuhani.
sw.R: Baadaye uvimbe mweupe au doa linalong'aa, jeupe lenye rangi ya waridi, linaweza kutokea mahali lilipokuwa jipu. Basi lazima mtu huyo amwonyeshe kuhani.

decisions.choice: reddish-white: white with a tinge of red
decisions.reason: The repeated syllables of the color word make it faint, 'reddish', as in verses 24, 42-43 and 49. The spot is white touched with red.

decisions.choice: pinkish-white
decisions.reason: Readable says 'pinkish-white' for white with a faint red, here and in verses 24, 42 and 43.

source.text: וְרָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה מַרְאֶ֨הָ֙ שָׁפָ֣ל מִן־הָע֔וֹר וּשְׂעָרָ֖הּ הָפַ֣ךְ לָבָ֑ן וְטִמְּא֧וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֛ן נֶֽגַע־צָרַ֥עַת הִ֖וא בַּשְּׁחִ֥ין פָּרָֽחָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will see the priest, and there! its appearance [is] low more than the skin, and its hair has turned white, then will pronounce him unclean the priest; [a] mark of scale disease it [is]; in the boil it has broken out.

en.L: And the priest shall look, and there! its appearance [is] lower than the skin, and its hair has turned white; then the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it [is] a mark of scale disease; it has broken out in the boil.
en.B: The priest is to examine it. If it looks lower than the skin around it and its hair has turned white, the priest is to declare the person unclean. It is a sore of serious skin disease that has broken out where the boil was.
en.R: The priest must look at it. It may seem lower than the skin around it, and the hair in it may have turned white. Then the priest must say that the person is unclean. A serious skin disease has broken out where the boil was.

es.L: Y el sacerdote mirará, y he aquí, su aspecto [es] más bajo que la piel, y su pelo se ha vuelto blanco; entonces el sacerdote lo declarará impuro; marca de enfermedad de la piel [es]; en el forúnculo ha brotado.
es.B: El sacerdote la examinará. Si parece más hundida que la piel de alrededor y su pelo se ha vuelto blanco, el sacerdote declarará impura a la persona. Es una llaga de enfermedad grave de la piel que ha brotado donde estaba el forúnculo.
es.R: El sacerdote tiene que mirarla. Puede que parezca más hundida que la piel de alrededor, y que el pelo que hay en ella se haya vuelto blanco. Entonces el sacerdote tiene que decir que la persona es impura. Ha brotado una enfermedad grave de la piel donde estaba el forúnculo.

fr.L: Et le prêtre regardera, et voici, son aspect [est] plus bas que la peau, et son poil est devenu blanc ; alors le prêtre le déclarera impur ; c’[est] une marque de maladie de peau ; elle a éclaté dans le furoncle.
fr.B: Le prêtre l’examinera. Si elle paraît plus basse que la peau qui l’entoure et que son poil est devenu blanc, le prêtre déclarera la personne impure. C’est une lésion de maladie de peau grave qui s’est déclarée là où était le furoncle.
fr.R: Le prêtre doit la regarder. Elle semble peut-être plus basse que la peau autour, et les poils qui s’y trouvent sont peut-être devenus blancs. Alors le prêtre doit dire que la personne est impure. Une maladie de peau grave s’est déclarée là où était le furoncle.

sw.L: Na kuhani ataangalia, na tazama, sura yake [ni] ya chini zaidi kuliko ngozi, na nywele zake zimegeuka kuwa nyeupe; ndipo kuhani atamtangaza kuwa najisi; ni alama ya ugonjwa wa ngozi; imechipuka katika jipu.
sw.B: Kuhani ataliangalia. Ikiwa linaonekana kuwa chini zaidi kuliko ngozi inayolizunguka na nywele zake zimekuwa nyeupe, kuhani atamtangaza mtu huyo kuwa najisi. Ni kidonda cha ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi kilichochipuka mahali lilipokuwa jipu.
sw.R: Lazima kuhani aliangalie. Huenda likaonekana kuwa chini zaidi kuliko ngozi inayolizunguka, na nywele zilizo ndani yake zimekuwa nyeupe. Basi lazima kuhani aseme kwamba mtu huyo ni najisi. Ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi umechipuka mahali lilipokuwa jipu.

decisions.choice: lower than the skin: sunk below the surface
decisions.reason: This word means 'low'. It gives the same sign as 'deep' in verse 3.

decisions.choice: broken out: appeared and grown, as in verse 12
decisions.reason: The disease has come up in the healed place of the boil.

source.text: וְאִ֣ם׀יִרְאֶ֣נָּה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵֽין־בָּהּ֙ שֵׂעָ֣ר לָבָ֔ן וּשְׁפָלָ֥ה אֵינֶ֛נָּה מִן־הָע֖וֹר וְהִ֣יא כֵהָ֑ה וְהִסְגִּיר֥וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And if will see it the priest, and there! not [is] in it hair white, and low it [is] not more than the skin, and it [is] faint, then will shut him up the priest seven days.

en.L: But if the priest looks at it, and there! there [is] no white hair in it, and it [is] not lower than the skin, and it [is] faint, then the priest shall shut him up seven days.
en.B: But if the priest finds no white hair in it, and it is not lower than the skin, and it has faded, he is to shut the person away for seven days.
en.R: But the priest may find that there is no white hair in it, and it is not lower than the skin, and it has become pale. Then he must keep the person away from others for seven days.

es.L: Pero si el sacerdote la mira, y he aquí, no [hay] en ella pelo blanco, y no [es] más baja que la piel, y [está] apagada, el sacerdote lo encerrará siete días.
es.B: Pero si el sacerdote no encuentra en ella pelo blanco, y no está más hundida que la piel, y ha perdido color, aislará a la persona durante siete días.
es.R: Pero puede que el sacerdote vea que no hay pelo blanco en ella, que no está más hundida que la piel y que se ha puesto pálida. Entonces tiene que mantener a la persona apartada de los demás durante siete días.

fr.L: Mais si le prêtre la regarde, et voici, il n’y [a] pas de poil blanc en elle, et elle n’[est] pas plus basse que la peau, et elle [est] terne, le prêtre l’enfermera sept jours.
fr.B: Mais si le prêtre n’y trouve pas de poil blanc, qu’elle n’est pas plus basse que la peau et qu’elle a pâli, il isolera la personne pendant sept jours.
fr.R: Mais le prêtre peut voir qu’il n’y a pas de poils blancs dedans, qu’elle n’est pas plus basse que la peau et qu’elle est devenue pâle. Alors il doit tenir la personne à l’écart des autres pendant sept jours.

sw.L: Lakini kuhani akiliangalia, na tazama, hakuna nywele nyeupe ndani yake, nalo si la chini zaidi kuliko ngozi, nalo limefifia, kuhani atamfungia siku saba.
sw.B: Lakini kuhani asipoona nywele nyeupe ndani yake, nalo halijashuka chini ya ngozi, nalo limefifia, atamtenga mtu huyo kwa siku saba.
sw.R: Lakini huenda kuhani akaona kwamba hakuna nywele nyeupe ndani yake, na halionekani kuwa chini zaidi kuliko ngozi, tena limepauka. Basi lazima amweke mtu huyo mbali na watu wengine kwa siku saba.

decisions.choice: faint, so shut up: a doubtful case, so a week of waiting
decisions.reason: As in verse 4. Here only one week is given before the ruling (verses 22-23).

source.text: וְאִם־פָּשֹׂ֥ה תִפְשֶׂ֖ה בָּע֑וֹר וְטִמֵּ֧א הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֹת֖וֹ נֶ֥גַע הִֽוא׃

records.literal_gloss: And if indeed it will spread in the skin, then will pronounce him unclean the priest; [a] mark it [is].

en.L: And if it indeed spreads in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it [is] a mark.
en.B: If it spreads in the skin, the priest is to declare the person unclean. It is a sore of the disease.
en.R: If it spreads on the skin, the priest must say that the person is unclean. It is a sore from the disease.

es.L: Y si en verdad se extiende en la piel, el sacerdote lo declarará impuro; marca [es].
es.B: Si se extiende por la piel, el sacerdote declarará impura a la persona. Es una llaga de la enfermedad.
es.R: Si se extiende por la piel, el sacerdote tiene que decir que la persona es impura. Es una llaga de la enfermedad.

fr.L: Et si elle s’étend vraiment sur la peau, le prêtre le déclarera impur ; c’[est] une marque.
fr.B: Si elle s’étend sur la peau, le prêtre déclarera la personne impure. C’est une lésion de la maladie.
fr.R: Si elle s’étend sur la peau, le prêtre doit dire que la personne est impure. C’est une plaie de la maladie.

sw.L: Na likienea kweli katika ngozi, kuhani atamtangaza kuwa najisi; ni alama.
sw.B: Likienea katika ngozi, kuhani atamtangaza mtu huyo kuwa najisi. Ni kidonda cha ugonjwa huo.
sw.R: Likienea kwenye ngozi, lazima kuhani aseme kwamba mtu huyo ni najisi. Ni kidonda cha ugonjwa huo.

decisions.choice: it is a mark: a mark of the disease
decisions.reason: 'Mark' alone is short for 'mark of scale disease', as verse 20 has it in full.

decisions.choice: of the disease
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add 'of the disease' so that 'sore' is not read as any sore at all.

source.text: וְאִם־תַּחְתֶּ֜יהָ תַּעֲמֹ֤ד הַבַּהֶ֨רֶת֙ לֹ֣א פָשָׂ֔תָה צָרֶ֥בֶת הַשְּׁחִ֖ין הִ֑וא וְטִהֲר֖וֹ הַכֹּהֵֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And if in its place will stay the bright spot, not it has spread, [the] scar of the boil it [is]; and will pronounce him clean the priest.

en.L: But if the bright spot stays in its place [and] has not spread, it [is] the scar of the boil; and the priest shall pronounce him clean.
en.B: If the bright spot stays put and does not spread, it is the boil's scar, and the priest is to declare the person clean.
en.R: But the shiny spot may stay the same and not spread. Then it is only a scar left by the boil. The priest must say that the person is clean.

es.L: Pero si en su lugar se queda la mancha brillante, [y] no se ha extendido, cicatriz del forúnculo [es]; y el sacerdote lo declarará puro.
es.B: Si la mancha brillante se queda donde está y no se extiende, es la cicatriz del forúnculo, y el sacerdote declarará pura a la persona.
es.R: Pero puede que la mancha que brilla siga igual y no se extienda. Entonces es solo una cicatriz que dejó el forúnculo. El sacerdote tiene que decir que la persona es pura.

fr.L: Mais si la tache brillante reste à sa place [et] ne s’est pas étendue, c’[est] la cicatrice du furoncle ; et le prêtre le déclarera pur.
fr.B: Si la tache brillante reste où elle est et ne s’étend pas, c’est la cicatrice du furoncle, et le prêtre déclarera la personne pure.
fr.R: Mais la tache qui brille peut rester la même et ne pas s’étendre. Alors ce n’est qu’une cicatrice laissée par le furoncle. Le prêtre doit dire que la personne est pure.

sw.L: Lakini doa linalong'aa likikaa mahali pake, [na] halijaenea, ni kovu la jipu; na kuhani atamtangaza kuwa safi.
sw.B: Doa linalong'aa likibaki pale pale bila kuenea, ni kovu la jipu, na kuhani atamtangaza mtu huyo kuwa safi.
sw.R: Lakini huenda doa linalong'aa likabaki vilevile bila kuenea. Basi ni kovu tu lililoachwa na jipu. Lazima kuhani aseme kwamba mtu huyo ni safi.

decisions.choice: scar: the mark left by the healed boil
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb for burning or scorching, and names the scarred or inflamed skin where the boil has healed. Verse 28 uses it of a burn.

source.text: א֣וֹ בָשָׂ֔ר כִּֽי־יִהְיֶ֥ה בְעֹר֖וֹ מִכְוַת־אֵ֑שׁ וְֽהָיְתָ֞ה מִֽחְיַ֣ת הַמִּכְוָ֗ה בַּהֶ֛רֶת לְבָנָ֥ה אֲדַמְדֶּ֖מֶת א֥וֹ לְבָנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Or flesh, when will be in its skin [a] burn of fire, and will be the raw spot of the burn [a] bright spot white reddish or white,

en.L: Or [as for] flesh, when there is in its skin a burn of fire, and the raw spot of the burn becomes a reddish-white or white bright spot,
en.B: Or when someone has a burn on their skin, and the raw place of the burn becomes a reddish-white or white bright spot,
en.R: Someone may get burned on their skin. Then a pinkish-white or white shiny spot may appear in the raw place where the burn was.

es.L: O [en cuanto a] la carne, cuando haya en su piel una quemadura de fuego, y el punto en carne viva de la quemadura se vuelva una mancha brillante blanca rojiza o blanca,
es.B: O cuando alguien tenga una quemadura en la piel, y la parte en carne viva de la quemadura se convierta en una mancha brillante de color blanco rojizo o blanco,
es.R: Puede que alguien se queme la piel. Después puede aparecer una mancha que brilla, de color blanco rosado o blanco, en la parte en carne viva donde estaba la quemadura.

fr.L: Ou [quant à] la chair, lorsqu’il y aura sur sa peau une brûlure de feu, et que la chair vive de la brûlure deviendra une tache brillante d’un blanc rougeâtre ou blanche,
fr.B: Ou lorsque quelqu’un a une brûlure sur la peau, et que la chair vive de la brûlure devient une tache brillante d’un blanc rougeâtre ou blanche,
fr.R: Il peut arriver qu’une personne se brûle la peau. Ensuite, une tache qui brille, d’un blanc rosé ou blanche, peut apparaître sur la chair vive, à l’endroit de la brûlure.

sw.L: Au [kuhusu] mwili, utakapokuwa na jeraha la kuungua kwa moto katika ngozi yake, na sehemu ya nyama hai ya jeraha hilo ikawa doa linalong'aa jeupe lenye wekundu au jeupe,
sw.B: Au mtu akiwa na jeraha la kuungua kwenye ngozi yake, na sehemu mbichi ya jeraha hilo ikawa doa linalong'aa jeupe lenye wekundu au jeupe,
sw.R: Huenda mtu akaungua kwenye ngozi yake. Kisha doa linalong'aa, jeupe lenye rangi ya waridi au jeupe, linaweza kutokea kwenye sehemu mbichi alipoungua.

decisions.choice: a burn of fire: a burn on the skin
decisions.reason: The noun appears only in verses 24-28. 'Of fire' makes clear that it is a burn from heat. As with the boil (verse 18), the burn itself is not unclean; the question is what forms on it as it heals.

decisions.choice: the raw spot of the burn: the raw place where the skin was burned
decisions.reason: The same word as 'raw spot' in verse 10.

source.text: וְרָאָ֣ה אֹתָ֣הּ הַכֹּהֵ֡ן וְהִנֵּ֣ה נֶהְפַּךְ֩ שֵׂעָ֨ר לָבָ֜ן בַּבַּהֶ֗רֶת וּמַרְאֶ֨הָ֙ עָמֹ֣ק מִן־הָע֔וֹר צָרַ֣עַת הִ֔וא בַּמִּכְוָ֖ה פָּרָ֑חָה וְטִמֵּ֤א אֹתוֹ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן נֶ֥גַע צָרַ֖עַת הִֽוא׃

records.literal_gloss: and will see it the priest, and there! has been turned [the] hair white in the bright spot, and its appearance [is] deep more than the skin, scale disease it [is]; in the burn it has broken out; and will pronounce him unclean the priest; [a] mark of scale disease it [is].

en.L: then the priest shall look at it, and there! the hair in the bright spot has turned white, and its appearance [is] deeper than the skin; it [is] scale disease; it has broken out in the burn; and the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it [is] a mark of scale disease.
en.B: the priest is to look at it. If the hair in the bright spot has turned white and the spot looks deeper than the skin, it is a serious skin disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest is to declare the person unclean; it is a sore of serious skin disease.
en.R: The priest must look at it. The hair in the spot may have turned white, and the spot may seem to go deeper than the skin. Then a serious skin disease has broken out in the burn. The priest must say that the person is unclean. It is a sore from a serious skin disease.

es.L: y el sacerdote la mirará, y he aquí, el pelo en la mancha brillante se ha vuelto blanco, y su aspecto [es] más profundo que la piel; enfermedad de la piel [es]; en la quemadura ha brotado; y el sacerdote lo declarará impuro; marca de enfermedad de la piel [es].
es.B: el sacerdote la examinará. Si el pelo de la mancha brillante se ha vuelto blanco y la mancha parece más honda que la piel, es una enfermedad grave de la piel que ha brotado en la quemadura. El sacerdote declarará impura a la persona; es una llaga de enfermedad grave de la piel.
es.R: El sacerdote tiene que mirarla. Puede que el pelo de la mancha se haya vuelto blanco, y que la mancha parezca más honda que la piel. Entonces ha brotado una enfermedad grave de la piel en la quemadura. El sacerdote tiene que decir que la persona es impura. Es una llaga de una enfermedad grave de la piel.

fr.L: alors le prêtre la regardera, et voici, le poil de la tache brillante est devenu blanc, et son aspect [est] plus profond que la peau ; c’[est] une maladie de peau ; elle a éclaté dans la brûlure ; et le prêtre le déclarera impur ; c’[est] une marque de maladie de peau.
fr.B: le prêtre l’examinera. Si le poil de la tache brillante est devenu blanc et que la tache paraît plus profonde que la peau, c’est une maladie de peau grave qui s’est déclarée dans la brûlure. Le prêtre déclarera la personne impure : c’est une lésion de maladie de peau grave.
fr.R: Le prêtre doit la regarder. Les poils de la tache sont peut-être devenus blancs, et la tache semble peut-être plus profonde que la peau. Alors une maladie de peau grave s’est déclarée dans la brûlure. Le prêtre doit dire que la personne est impure. C’est la plaie d’une maladie de peau grave.

sw.L: ndipo kuhani ataliangalia, na tazama, nywele katika doa linalong'aa zimegeuka kuwa nyeupe, na sura yake [ni] ya ndani zaidi kuliko ngozi; ni ugonjwa wa ngozi; umechipuka katika jeraha la kuungua; na kuhani atamtangaza kuwa najisi; ni alama ya ugonjwa wa ngozi.
sw.B: kuhani ataliangalia. Ikiwa nywele katika doa linalong'aa zimekuwa nyeupe na doa hilo linaonekana kuingia ndani zaidi ya ngozi, ni ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi uliochipuka katika jeraha la kuungua. Kuhani atamtangaza mtu huyo kuwa najisi; ni kidonda cha ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi.
sw.R: Lazima kuhani aliangalie. Huenda nywele zilizo katika doa hilo zimekuwa nyeupe, na doa linaonekana kuingia ndani zaidi ya ngozi. Basi ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi umechipuka mahali alipoungua. Lazima kuhani aseme kwamba mtu huyo ni najisi. Ni kidonda cha ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi.

decisions.choice: white hair and depth: the same two signs as in verse 3
decisions.reason: The burn is judged as the boil was (verse 20): white hair in the spot and a look of depth show the disease.

source.text: וְאִ֣ם׀יִרְאֶ֣נָּה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵֽין־בַּבֶּהֶ֨רֶת֙ שֵׂעָ֣ר לָבָ֔ן וּשְׁפָלָ֥ה אֵינֶ֛נָּה מִן־הָע֖וֹר וְהִ֣וא כֵהָ֑ה וְהִסְגִּיר֥וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And if will see it the priest, and there! not [is] in the bright spot hair white, and low it [is] not more than the skin, and it [is] faint, then will shut him up the priest seven days.

en.L: But if the priest looks at it, and there! there [is] no white hair in the bright spot, and it [is] not lower than the skin, and it [is] faint, then the priest shall shut him up seven days.
en.B: But if the priest finds no white hair in the bright spot, and it is not lower than the skin, and it has faded, he is to shut the person away for seven days.
en.R: But the priest may find no white hair in the spot. It may not be lower than the skin, and it may have become pale. Then he must keep the person away from others for seven days.

es.L: Pero si el sacerdote la mira, y he aquí, no [hay] en la mancha brillante pelo blanco, y no [es] más baja que la piel, y [está] apagada, el sacerdote lo encerrará siete días.
es.B: Pero si el sacerdote no encuentra pelo blanco en la mancha brillante, y no está más hundida que la piel, y ha perdido color, aislará a la persona durante siete días.
es.R: Pero puede que el sacerdote no encuentre pelo blanco en la mancha. Puede que no esté más hundida que la piel y que se haya puesto pálida. Entonces tiene que mantener a la persona apartada de los demás durante siete días.

fr.L: Mais si le prêtre la regarde, et voici, il n’y [a] pas de poil blanc dans la tache brillante, et elle n’[est] pas plus basse que la peau, et elle [est] terne, le prêtre l’enfermera sept jours.
fr.B: Mais si le prêtre ne trouve pas de poil blanc dans la tache brillante, qu’elle n’est pas plus basse que la peau et qu’elle a pâli, il isolera la personne pendant sept jours.
fr.R: Mais le prêtre peut ne trouver aucun poil blanc dans la tache. Elle n’est peut-être pas plus basse que la peau, et elle est peut-être devenue pâle. Alors il doit tenir la personne à l’écart des autres pendant sept jours.

sw.L: Lakini kuhani akiliangalia, na tazama, hakuna nywele nyeupe katika doa linalong'aa, nalo si la chini zaidi kuliko ngozi, nalo limefifia, kuhani atamfungia siku saba.
sw.B: Lakini kuhani asipoona nywele nyeupe katika doa linalong'aa, nalo halijashuka chini ya ngozi, nalo limefifia, atamtenga mtu huyo kwa siku saba.
sw.R: Lakini huenda kuhani asione nywele nyeupe katika doa hilo. Huenda doa lisiwe chini zaidi kuliko ngozi, tena limepauka. Basi lazima amweke mtu huyo mbali na watu wengine kwa siku saba.

decisions.choice: as with the boil: the same doubtful case as verse 21
decisions.reason: Where the signs are missing, the priest waits a week before ruling (verse 4).

source.text: וְרָאָ֥הוּ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֑י אִם־פָּשֹׂ֤ה תִפְשֶׂה֙ בָּע֔וֹר וְטִמֵּ֤א הַכֹּהֵן֙ אֹת֔וֹ נֶ֥גַע צָרַ֖עַת הִֽוא׃

records.literal_gloss: And will see him the priest on the seventh day; if indeed it will spread in the skin, then will pronounce him unclean the priest; [a] mark of scale disease it [is].

en.L: And the priest shall look at him on the seventh day; if it indeed spreads in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it [is] a mark of scale disease.
en.B: On the seventh day the priest is to look at them. If it has spread in the skin, the priest is to declare the person unclean; it is a sore of serious skin disease.
en.R: On the seventh day the priest must look at the person again. If the spot has spread on the skin, he must say that the person is unclean. It is a sore from a serious skin disease.

es.L: Y el sacerdote lo mirará el séptimo día; si en verdad se extiende en la piel, el sacerdote lo declarará impuro; marca de enfermedad de la piel [es].
es.B: El séptimo día el sacerdote la examinará. Si se ha extendido por la piel, el sacerdote declarará impura a la persona; es una llaga de enfermedad grave de la piel.
es.R: El séptimo día el sacerdote tiene que mirar otra vez a la persona. Si la mancha se ha extendido por la piel, tiene que decir que la persona es impura. Es una llaga de una enfermedad grave de la piel.

fr.L: Et le prêtre le regardera le septième jour ; si elle s’étend vraiment sur la peau, le prêtre le déclarera impur ; c’[est] une marque de maladie de peau.
fr.B: Le septième jour, le prêtre examinera la personne. Si la tache s’est étendue sur la peau, le prêtre la déclarera impure : c’est une lésion de maladie de peau grave.
fr.R: Le septième jour, le prêtre doit regarder la personne encore une fois. Si la tache s’est étendue sur la peau, il doit dire que la personne est impure. C’est la plaie d’une maladie de peau grave.

sw.L: Na kuhani atamwangalia siku ya saba; likienea kweli katika ngozi, kuhani atamtangaza kuwa najisi; ni alama ya ugonjwa wa ngozi.
sw.B: Siku ya saba kuhani atamwangalia. Ikiwa doa limeenea katika ngozi, kuhani atamtangaza mtu huyo kuwa najisi; ni kidonda cha ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi.
sw.R: Siku ya saba lazima kuhani amwangalie mtu huyo tena. Ikiwa doa limeenea kwenye ngozi, lazima aseme kwamba mtu huyo ni najisi. Ni kidonda cha ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi.

decisions.choice: indeed spreads: if it really has spread
decisions.reason: The doubled verb, as in verse 7.

source.text: וְאִם־תַּחְתֶּיהָ֩ תַעֲמֹ֨ד הַבַּהֶ֜רֶת לֹא־פָשְׂתָ֤ה בָעוֹר֙ וְהִ֣וא כֵהָ֔ה שְׂאֵ֥ת הַמִּכְוָ֖ה הִ֑וא וְטִֽהֲרוֹ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן כִּֽי־צָרֶ֥בֶת הַמִּכְוָ֖ה הִֽוא׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And if in its place will stay the bright spot, not it has spread in the skin, and it [is] faint, [the] swelling of the burn it [is]; and will pronounce him clean the priest, for [the] scar of the burn it [is].

en.L: But if the bright spot stays in its place [and] has not spread in the skin, and it [is] faint, it [is] the swelling of the burn; and the priest shall pronounce him clean, for it [is] the scar of the burn.
en.B: But if the bright spot stays where it is, has not spread in the skin, and has faded, it is the swelling from the burn. The priest is to declare the person clean, because it is the scar of the burn.
en.R: But the shiny spot may stay the same, without spreading, and become pale. Then it is only swelling from the burn. The priest must say that the person is clean, because it is the scar left by the burn.

es.L: Pero si en su lugar se queda la mancha brillante, [y] no se ha extendido en la piel, y [está] apagada, hinchazón de la quemadura [es]; y el sacerdote lo declarará puro, porque cicatriz de la quemadura [es].
es.B: Pero si la mancha brillante se queda donde está, no se ha extendido por la piel y ha perdido color, es la hinchazón de la quemadura. El sacerdote declarará pura a la persona, porque es la cicatriz de la quemadura.
