es.R: Pero puede que la mancha que brilla siga igual, sin extenderse, y se ponga pálida. Entonces es solo la hinchazón de la quemadura. El sacerdote tiene que decir que la persona es pura, porque es la cicatriz que dejó la quemadura.

fr.L: Mais si la tache brillante reste à sa place [et] ne s’est pas étendue sur la peau, et [si] elle [est] terne, c’[est] l’enflure de la brûlure ; et le prêtre le déclarera pur, car c’[est] la cicatrice de la brûlure.
fr.B: Mais si la tache brillante reste où elle est, ne s’est pas étendue sur la peau et a pâli, c’est l’enflure de la brûlure. Le prêtre déclarera la personne pure, car c’est la cicatrice de la brûlure.
fr.R: Mais la tache qui brille peut rester la même, sans s’étendre, et devenir pâle. Alors ce n’est que l’enflure de la brûlure. Le prêtre doit dire que la personne est pure, car c’est la cicatrice laissée par la brûlure.

sw.L: Lakini doa linalong'aa likikaa mahali pake, [na] halijaenea katika ngozi, nalo limefifia, ni uvimbe wa jeraha la kuungua; na kuhani atamtangaza kuwa safi, kwa maana ni kovu la jeraha la kuungua.
sw.B: Lakini doa linalong'aa likibaki pale pale, bila kuenea katika ngozi, nalo limefifia, ni uvimbe wa jeraha la kuungua. Kuhani atamtangaza mtu huyo kuwa safi, kwa sababu ni kovu la jeraha hilo.
sw.R: Lakini huenda doa linalong'aa likabaki vilevile bila kuenea, tena likapauka. Basi ni uvimbe tu wa mahali alipoungua. Lazima kuhani aseme kwamba mtu huyo ni safi, kwa sababu ni kovu lililoachwa na jeraha la kuungua.

decisions.choice: the swelling, the scar of the burn: the normal marks of a healing burn
decisions.reason: As the scar of a boil is clean (verse 23), so is the scar of a burn.

source.text: וְאִישׁ֙ א֣וֹ אִשָּׁ֔ה כִּֽי־יִהְיֶ֥ה ב֖וֹ נָ֑גַע בְּרֹ֖אשׁ א֥וֹ בְזָקָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And [a] man or [a] woman, when will be on him [a] mark on [the] head or in [the] beard,

en.L: And a man or a woman, when there is a mark on him, on the head or in the beard,
en.B: When a man or a woman has a sore on the head or in the beard,
en.R: A man or a woman may have a sore on the head, or a man may have one in his beard.

es.L: Y un hombre o una mujer, cuando haya en él una marca en la cabeza o en la barba,
es.B: Cuando un hombre o una mujer tenga una llaga en la cabeza o en la barba,
es.R: Un hombre o una mujer puede tener una llaga en la cabeza, o un hombre puede tenerla en la barba.

fr.L: Et un homme ou une femme, lorsqu’il y aura sur lui une marque, sur la tête ou dans la barbe,
fr.B: Lorsqu’un homme ou une femme a une lésion sur la tête ou dans la barbe,
fr.R: Un homme ou une femme peut avoir une plaie sur la tête, ou un homme peut en avoir une dans la barbe.

sw.L: Na mwanamume au mwanamke, atakapokuwa na alama, kichwani au katika ndevu,
sw.B: Mwanamume au mwanamke akiwa na kidonda kichwani au katika ndevu,
sw.R: Mwanamume au mwanamke anaweza kuwa na kidonda kichwani, au mwanamume anaweza kuwa nacho katika ndevu zake.

decisions.choice: a man or a woman: the law names both
decisions.reason: This case names both; the beard applies to men and the head to both. The Hebrew goes on with 'him', as it does for any person.

decisions.choice: head or beard: a mark where hair grows
decisions.reason: Verses 29-37 deal with marks in the hair of the head and chin, where the signs differ from those on bare skin: thin yellow hair, not white (verse 30).

decisions.choice: a man ... in his beard
decisions.reason: Readable says that the beard concerns men.

source.text: וְרָאָ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֶת־הַנֶּ֗גַע וְהִנֵּ֤ה מַרְאֵ֨הוּ֙ עָמֹ֣ק מִן־הָע֔וֹר וּב֛וֹ שֵׂעָ֥ר צָהֹ֖ב דָּ֑ק וְטִמֵּ֨א אֹת֤וֹ הַכֹּהֵן֙ נֶ֣תֶק ה֔וּא צָרַ֧עַת הָרֹ֛אשׁ א֥וֹ הַזָּקָ֖ן הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: then will see the priest the mark, and there! its appearance [is] deep more than the skin, and in it [is] hair yellow thin, then will pronounce him unclean the priest; [a] scall it [is], scale disease of the head or of the beard it [is].

en.L: then the priest shall look at the mark, and there! its appearance [is] deeper than the skin, and in it [is] thin yellow hair; then the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it [is] a scall; it [is] scale disease of the head or of the beard.
en.B: the priest is to examine the sore. If it looks deeper than the skin and there is thin yellow hair in it, the priest is to declare the person unclean. It is a scaly itch, a serious skin disease of the head or beard.
en.R: The priest must look at the sore. It may seem to go deeper than the skin, with thin yellow hair in it. Then the priest must say that the person is unclean. It is an itchy, scaly patch, a serious skin disease of the head or chin.

es.L: el sacerdote mirará la marca, y he aquí, su aspecto [es] más profundo que la piel, y en ella [hay] pelo amarillo y fino; entonces el sacerdote lo declarará impuro; tiña [es], enfermedad de la piel de la cabeza o de la barba [es].
es.B: el sacerdote examinará la llaga. Si parece más honda que la piel y hay en ella pelo amarillo y fino, el sacerdote declarará impura a la persona. Es una erupción escamosa, una enfermedad grave de la piel de la cabeza o de la barba.
es.R: El sacerdote tiene que mirar la llaga. Puede que parezca más honda que la piel, con pelo amarillo y fino en ella. Entonces el sacerdote tiene que decir que la persona es impura. Es una zona que pica y se pela, una enfermedad grave de la piel de la cabeza o del mentón.

fr.L: le prêtre regardera la marque, et voici, son aspect [est] plus profond que la peau, et il y [a] en elle du poil jaune et fin ; alors le prêtre le déclarera impur ; c’[est] la teigne ; c’[est] une maladie de peau de la tête ou de la barbe.
fr.B: le prêtre examinera la lésion. Si elle paraît plus profonde que la peau et qu’il s’y trouve des poils jaunes et fins, le prêtre déclarera la personne impure. C’est une dartre, une maladie de peau grave de la tête ou de la barbe.
fr.R: Le prêtre doit regarder la plaie. Elle semble peut-être plus profonde que la peau, avec des poils jaunes et fins dedans. Alors le prêtre doit dire que la personne est impure. C’est une plaque qui démange et qui pèle, une maladie de peau grave de la tête ou du menton.

sw.L: kuhani ataiangalia alama, na tazama, sura yake [ni] ya ndani zaidi kuliko ngozi, na ndani yake [kuna] nywele za manjano nyembamba; ndipo kuhani atamtangaza kuwa najisi; ni choa; ni ugonjwa wa ngozi wa kichwa au wa ndevu.
sw.B: kuhani atakichunguza kidonda. Ikiwa kinaonekana kuingia ndani zaidi ya ngozi na kuna nywele za manjano nyembamba ndani yake, kuhani atamtangaza mtu huyo kuwa najisi. Ni choa, ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi wa kichwa au wa ndevu.
sw.R: Lazima kuhani akiangalie kidonda. Huenda kikaonekana kuingia ndani zaidi ya ngozi, na kuna nywele za manjano nyembamba ndani yake. Basi lazima kuhani aseme kwamba mtu huyo ni najisi. Ni sehemu inayowasha na kubanduka magamba, ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi wa kichwa au wa kidevu.

decisions.choice: scall: a scaly, itching patch on the scalp or chin
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to tear away or pull out, perhaps for the scratching it causes or the hair it loosens. It names a disease of the parts of the body where hair grows, judged apart from marks on bare skin. Its exact nature is not known.

decisions.choice: thin yellow hair: sparse hair that has turned gold or yellow
decisions.reason: In the hair of the head or beard this is the sign of the disease, as white hair is on the skin (verse 3). Black hair is the sign of health (verses 31 and 37).

decisions.choice: a scaly itch / an itchy, scaly patch; chin
decisions.reason: Literal keeps 'scall', an old English word for a scaly disease of the scalp, one word for the one Hebrew term. Balanced and Readable describe it in common words, as 14:54 does. Readable says 'chin' for the beard, as there.

decisions.choice: "tiña" (L); "erupción escamosa" (B); "zona que pica y se pela", then "zona que pica" (R)
decisions.reason: "Tiña" is the old Spanish name for a scaly disease of the scalp, and stands at Literal for the one Hebrew term, as the English keeps "scall". It names a known fungal infection, so Balanced and Readable describe the patch instead, as the English does. "Costra" is kept for the scab of verse 2.

decisions.choice: "la teigne" (L); "une dartre" (B); "une plaque qui démange et qui pèle", then "la plaque qui démange" (R)
decisions.reason: "Teigne" is the old French name for a scaly disease of the scalp, and stands at Literal for the one Hebrew term, as the English keeps "scall". Balanced says "dartre", the ordinary word for a scaly patch of skin; Readable describes it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "choa" (L, B); "sehemu inayowasha na kubanduka magamba", then "sehemu inayowasha" (R)
decisions.reason: "Choa" is the Swahili name for a scaly, itching disease of the scalp and skin, close to what the Hebrew word describes, so Literal and Balanced keep it. Readable describes the patch, as the English does. "Upele" is kept for the harmless rash of verse 39.

source.text: וְכִֽי־יִרְאֶ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֶת־נֶ֣גַע הַנֶּ֗תֶק וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵין־מַרְאֵ֨הוּ֙ עָמֹ֣ק מִן־הָע֔וֹר וְשֵׂעָ֥ר שָׁחֹ֖ר אֵ֣ין בּ֑וֹ וְהִסְגִּ֧יר הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֶת־נֶ֥גַע הַנֶּ֖תֶק שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And when will see the priest the mark of the scall, and there! not its appearance [is] deep more than the skin, and hair black not [is] in it, then will shut up the priest the [one with the] mark of the scall seven days.

en.L: And if the priest looks at the mark of the scall, and there! its appearance [is] not deeper than the skin, and there [is] no black hair in it, then the priest shall shut up the [one with the] mark of the scall seven days.
en.B: But if the priest examines the sore of the scaly itch and it does not look deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, he is to shut the person with the sore away for seven days.
en.R: But when the priest looks at the itchy patch, it may not seem to go deeper than the skin. And there may be no black hair in it. Then the priest must keep the person away from others for seven days.

es.L: Y cuando el sacerdote mire la marca de la tiña, y he aquí, su aspecto no [es] más profundo que la piel, y no [hay] en ella pelo negro, el sacerdote encerrará [al que tiene] la marca de la tiña siete días.
es.B: Pero si el sacerdote examina la llaga de la erupción escamosa y no parece más honda que la piel, y no hay en ella pelo negro, aislará durante siete días a la persona que tiene la llaga.
es.R: Pero cuando el sacerdote mire la zona que pica, puede que no parezca más honda que la piel. Y puede que no haya pelo negro en ella. Entonces el sacerdote tiene que mantener a la persona apartada de los demás durante siete días.

fr.L: Et lorsque le prêtre regardera la marque de la teigne, et voici, son aspect n’[est] pas plus profond que la peau, et il n’y [a] pas en elle de poil noir, le prêtre enfermera [celui qui a] la marque de la teigne sept jours.
fr.B: Mais si le prêtre examine la lésion de la dartre et qu’elle ne paraît pas plus profonde que la peau, et qu’il n’y a pas de poil noir dedans, il isolera pendant sept jours la personne atteinte.
fr.R: Mais quand le prêtre regarde la plaque qui démange, elle ne semble peut-être pas plus profonde que la peau. Et il n’y a peut-être pas de poils noirs dedans. Alors le prêtre doit tenir la personne à l’écart des autres pendant sept jours.

sw.L: Na kuhani atakapoiangalia alama ya choa, na tazama, sura yake si ya ndani zaidi kuliko ngozi, na hakuna nywele nyeusi ndani yake, kuhani atamfungia [mwenye] alama ya choa siku saba.
sw.B: Lakini kuhani akikichunguza kidonda cha choa na hakionekani kuingia ndani zaidi ya ngozi, na hakuna nywele nyeusi ndani yake, atamtenga mtu mwenye kidonda hicho kwa siku saba.
sw.R: Lakini kuhani akiiangalia sehemu inayowasha, huenda isionekane kuingia ndani zaidi ya ngozi. Tena huenda hakuna nywele nyeusi ndani yake. Basi lazima kuhani amweke mtu huyo mbali na watu wengine kwa siku saba.

decisions.choice: no black hair: the healthy hair is missing
decisions.reason: Black was the normal color of hair, and black hair growing back shows healing (verse 37). With no sign of depth to confirm the disease and no black hair to rule it out, the case is doubtful, so the priest waits.

source.text: וְרָאָ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֣ן אֶת־הַנֶּגַע֮ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי֒ וְהִנֵּה֙ לֹא־פָשָׂ֣ה הַנֶּ֔תֶק וְלֹא־הָ֥יָה ב֖וֹ שֵׂעָ֣ר צָהֹ֑ב וּמַרְאֵ֣ה הַנֶּ֔תֶק אֵ֥ין עָמֹ֖ק מִן־הָעֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: And will see the priest the mark on the seventh day, and there! not has spread the scall, and not was in it hair yellow, and [the] appearance of the scall not [is] deep more than the skin,

en.L: And the priest shall look at the mark on the seventh day, and there! the scall has not spread, and there was no yellow hair in it, and the appearance of the scall [is] not deeper than the skin,
en.B: On the seventh day the priest is to look at the sore. If the scaly itch has not spread, and no yellow hair has appeared in it, and it does not look deeper than the skin,
en.R: On the seventh day the priest must look at the sore again. The itchy patch may not have spread. There may be no yellow hair in it, and it may not seem deeper than the skin.

es.L: Y el sacerdote mirará la marca el séptimo día, y he aquí, no se ha extendido la tiña, y no ha habido en ella pelo amarillo, y el aspecto de la tiña no [es] más profundo que la piel,
es.B: El séptimo día el sacerdote examinará la llaga. Si la erupción escamosa no se ha extendido, y no ha aparecido en ella pelo amarillo, y no parece más honda que la piel,
es.R: El séptimo día el sacerdote tiene que mirar otra vez la llaga. Puede que la zona que pica no se haya extendido. Puede que no haya pelo amarillo en ella, y que no parezca más honda que la piel.

fr.L: Et le prêtre regardera la marque le septième jour, et voici, la teigne ne s’est pas étendue, et il n’y a pas eu en elle de poil jaune, et l’aspect de la teigne n’[est] pas plus profond que la peau,
fr.B: Le septième jour, le prêtre examinera la lésion. Si la dartre ne s’est pas étendue, qu’aucun poil jaune n’y est apparu et qu’elle ne paraît pas plus profonde que la peau,
fr.R: Le septième jour, le prêtre doit regarder la plaie encore une fois. La plaque qui démange ne s’est peut-être pas étendue. Il n’y a peut-être pas de poils jaunes dedans, et elle ne semble peut-être pas plus profonde que la peau.

sw.L: Na kuhani ataiangalia alama siku ya saba, na tazama, choa haijaenea, wala hazikuwamo ndani yake nywele za manjano, na sura ya choa si ya ndani zaidi kuliko ngozi,
sw.B: Siku ya saba kuhani atakichunguza kidonda. Ikiwa choa haijaenea, wala hazijaota ndani yake nywele za manjano, wala haionekani kuingia ndani zaidi ya ngozi,
sw.R: Siku ya saba lazima kuhani akiangalie kidonda tena. Huenda sehemu inayowasha haijaenea. Huenda hakuna nywele za manjano ndani yake, wala haionekani kuingia ndani zaidi ya ngozi.

decisions.choice: not spread, no yellow hair, not deep: every sign is absent
decisions.reason: All three signs of the disease are missing, but the case is not yet closed (verse 33).

source.text: וְהִ֨תְגַּלָּ֔ח וְאֶת־הַנֶּ֖תֶק לֹ֣א יְגַלֵּ֑חַ וְהִסְגִּ֨יר הַכֹּהֵ֧ן אֶת־הַנֶּ֛תֶק שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים שֵׁנִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: then he will shave himself, but the scall not will he shave, and will shut up the priest the scall seven days [a] second [time].

en.L: then he shall shave himself, but the scall he shall not shave; and the priest shall shut up the [one with the] scall seven days a second [time].
en.B: the person is to shave, but not the place where the scaly itch is, and the priest is to shut them away for another seven days.
en.R: Then the person must shave off their hair, except on the itchy patch. The priest must keep them away from others for seven more days.

es.L: entonces él se rapará, pero la tiña no la rapará; y el sacerdote encerrará [al que tiene] la tiña siete días por segunda [vez].
es.B: la persona se afeitará, pero no el lugar donde está la erupción escamosa, y el sacerdote la aislará otros siete días.
es.R: Entonces la persona tiene que afeitarse el pelo, menos en la zona que pica. El sacerdote tiene que mantenerla apartada de los demás siete días más.

fr.L: alors il se rasera, mais la teigne, il ne la rasera pas ; et le prêtre enfermera [celui qui a] la teigne sept jours une seconde [fois].
fr.B: la personne se rasera, mais pas à l’endroit de la dartre, et le prêtre l’isolera encore sept jours.
fr.R: Alors la personne doit se raser, sauf sur la plaque qui démange. Le prêtre doit la tenir à l’écart des autres pendant sept jours de plus.

sw.L: ndipo atajinyoa, lakini choa hatainyoa; na kuhani atamfungia [mwenye] choa siku saba mara ya pili.
sw.B: mtu huyo atanyoa, lakini si mahali palipo na choa, na kuhani atamtenga kwa siku nyingine saba.
sw.R: Basi lazima mtu huyo anyoe nywele zake, isipokuwa kwenye sehemu inayowasha. Lazima kuhani amweke mbali na watu wengine kwa siku saba zaidi.

decisions.choice: shave himself, but not the scall: shave around the patch
decisions.reason: The person shaves the hair of the head or beard around the mark but leaves the hair on the mark itself. Then the priest can see clearly the next time whether it has spread and whether yellow hair grows in it.

decisions.choice: the scall: the person with the scall
decisions.reason: As 'mark' stands for the person in verse 4, here 'the scall' does.

source.text: וְרָאָה֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן אֶת־הַנֶּ֜תֶק בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י וְ֠הִנֵּה לֹא־פָשָׂ֤ה הַנֶּ֨תֶק֙ בָּע֔וֹר וּמַרְאֵ֕הוּ אֵינֶ֥נּוּ עָמֹ֖ק מִן־הָע֑וֹר וְטִהַ֤ר אֹתוֹ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְכִבֶּ֥ס בְּגָדָ֖יו וְטָהֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And will see the priest the scall on the seventh day, and there! not has spread the scall in the skin, and its appearance not [is] deep more than the skin, then will pronounce him clean the priest, and he will wash his garments and be clean.

en.L: And the priest shall look at the scall on the seventh day, and there! the scall has not spread in the skin, and its appearance [is] not deeper than the skin; then the priest shall pronounce him clean, and he shall wash his garments and be clean.
en.B: On the seventh day the priest is to look at the scaly itch. If it has not spread in the skin and does not look deeper than the skin, he is to declare the person clean. They must wash their clothes, and they will be clean.
en.R: On the seventh day the priest must look at the itchy patch. If it has not spread and does not seem deeper than the skin, he must say that the person is clean. The person must wash their clothes. Then they will be clean.

es.L: Y el sacerdote mirará la tiña el séptimo día, y he aquí, no se ha extendido la tiña en la piel, y su aspecto no [es] más profundo que la piel; entonces el sacerdote lo declarará puro, y lavará sus vestidos y será puro.
es.B: El séptimo día el sacerdote examinará la erupción escamosa. Si no se ha extendido por la piel y no parece más honda que la piel, declarará pura a la persona. Esta lavará su ropa y quedará pura.
es.R: El séptimo día el sacerdote tiene que mirar la zona que pica. Si no se ha extendido y no parece más honda que la piel, tiene que decir que la persona es pura. La persona tiene que lavar su ropa. Después quedará pura.

fr.L: Et le prêtre regardera la teigne le septième jour, et voici, la teigne ne s’est pas étendue sur la peau, et son aspect n’[est] pas plus profond que la peau ; alors le prêtre le déclarera pur, et il lavera ses vêtements et sera pur.
fr.B: Le septième jour, le prêtre examinera la dartre. Si elle ne s’est pas étendue sur la peau et ne paraît pas plus profonde que la peau, il déclarera la personne pure. Celle-ci lavera ses vêtements, et elle sera pure.
fr.R: Le septième jour, le prêtre doit regarder la plaque qui démange. Si elle ne s’est pas étendue et ne semble pas plus profonde que la peau, il doit dire que la personne est pure. La personne doit laver ses vêtements. Ensuite, elle sera pure.

sw.L: Na kuhani ataiangalia choa siku ya saba, na tazama, choa haijaenea katika ngozi, na sura yake si ya ndani zaidi kuliko ngozi; ndipo kuhani atamtangaza kuwa safi, naye atafua nguo zake na kuwa safi.
sw.B: Siku ya saba kuhani ataichunguza choa. Ikiwa haijaenea katika ngozi wala haionekani kuingia ndani zaidi ya ngozi, atamtangaza mtu huyo kuwa safi. Atafua nguo zake, naye atakuwa safi.
sw.R: Siku ya saba lazima kuhani aiangalie sehemu inayowasha. Ikiwa haijaenea wala haionekani kuingia ndani zaidi ya ngozi, lazima aseme kwamba mtu huyo ni safi. Lazima mtu huyo afue nguo zake. Kisha atakuwa safi.

decisions.choice: wash and be clean: see verse 6
decisions.reason: The washing closes the time of doubt.

source.text: וְאִם־פָּשֹׂ֥ה יִפְשֶׂ֛ה הַנֶּ֖תֶק בָּע֑וֹר אַחֲרֵ֖י טָהֳרָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And if indeed will spread the scall in the skin after his cleansing,

en.L: But if the scall indeed spreads in the skin after his cleansing,
en.B: But if the scaly itch does spread in the skin after they have been declared clean,
en.R: But the itchy patch may spread on the skin after the priest has said that the person is clean.

es.L: Pero si en verdad se extiende la tiña en la piel después de su purificación,
es.B: Pero si la erupción escamosa se extiende por la piel después de que la persona ha sido declarada pura,
es.R: Pero puede que la zona que pica se extienda por la piel después de que el sacerdote haya dicho que la persona es pura.

fr.L: Mais si la teigne s’étend vraiment sur la peau après sa purification,
fr.B: Mais si la dartre s’étend sur la peau après que la personne a été déclarée pure,
fr.R: Mais il arrive que la plaque qui démange s’étende sur la peau après que le prêtre a dit que la personne était pure.

sw.L: Lakini choa ikienea kweli katika ngozi baada ya kutakaswa kwake,
sw.B: Lakini choa ikienea katika ngozi baada ya mtu huyo kutangazwa kuwa safi,
sw.R: Lakini huenda sehemu inayowasha ikaenea kwenye ngozi baada ya kuhani kusema kwamba mtu huyo ni safi.

decisions.choice: after his cleansing: after the ruling of verse 34
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, the case can be opened again.

source.text: וְרָאָ֨הוּ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהִנֵּ֛ה פָּשָׂ֥ה הַנֶּ֖תֶק בָּע֑וֹר לֹֽא־יְבַקֵּ֧ר הַכֹּהֵ֛ן לַשֵּׂעָ֥ר הַצָּהֹ֖ב טָמֵ֥א הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: and will see him the priest, and there! has spread the scall in the skin, not will seek the priest for the hair yellow; unclean he [is].

en.L: and the priest looks at him, and there! the scall has spread in the skin, the priest shall not search for the yellow hair; he [is] unclean.
en.B: and the priest examines them and finds that it has spread in the skin, he need not look for yellow hair. The person is unclean.
en.R: If the priest sees that the patch has spread, he does not need to look for yellow hair. The person is unclean.

es.L: y el sacerdote lo mira, y he aquí, se ha extendido la tiña en la piel, el sacerdote no buscará el pelo amarillo; impuro [es].
es.B: y el sacerdote la examina y ve que se ha extendido por la piel, no hace falta que busque pelo amarillo. La persona es impura.
es.R: Si el sacerdote ve que la zona se ha extendido, no necesita buscar pelo amarillo. La persona es impura.

fr.L: et [si] le prêtre le regarde, et voici, la teigne s’est étendue sur la peau, le prêtre ne cherchera pas le poil jaune ; il [est] impur.
fr.B: et que le prêtre l’examine et constate qu’elle s’est étendue sur la peau, il n’a pas besoin de chercher de poil jaune. La personne est impure.
fr.R: Si le prêtre voit que la plaque s’est étendue, il n’a pas besoin de chercher des poils jaunes. La personne est impure.

sw.L: na kuhani amwangalie, na tazama, choa imeenea katika ngozi, kuhani hatatafuta nywele za manjano; yeye [ni] najisi.
sw.B: na kuhani akimchunguza na kuona kwamba imeenea katika ngozi, hana haja ya kutafuta nywele za manjano. Mtu huyo ni najisi.
sw.R: Kuhani akiona kwamba sehemu hiyo imeenea, hahitaji kutafuta nywele za manjano. Mtu huyo ni najisi.

decisions.choice: not search for the yellow hair: spreading alone settles it
decisions.reason: The spreading is enough to decide the case; the second sign (verse 30) need not be found.

source.text: וְאִם־בְּעֵינָיו֩ עָמַ֨ד הַנֶּ֜תֶק וְשֵׂעָ֨ר שָׁחֹ֧ר צָֽמַח־בּ֛וֹ נִרְפָּ֥א הַנֶּ֖תֶק טָה֣וֹר ה֑וּא וְטִהֲר֖וֹ הַכֹּהֵֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And if in his eyes has stood the scall, and hair black has sprouted in it, has been healed the scall; clean he [is]; and will pronounce him clean the priest.

en.L: But if in his eyes the scall has stood, and black hair has sprouted in it, the scall has been healed; he [is] clean; and the priest shall pronounce him clean.
en.B: But if in the priest's judgment the scaly itch is unchanged, and black hair has grown in it, it has healed. The person is clean, and the priest is to declare them clean.
en.R: But the priest may see that the itchy patch has stayed the same and black hair has grown in it. Then it has healed. The person is clean, and the priest must say so.

es.L: Pero si a sus ojos la tiña se ha mantenido, y ha brotado en ella pelo negro, la tiña se ha curado; puro [es]; y el sacerdote lo declarará puro.
es.B: Pero si a juicio del sacerdote la erupción escamosa sigue igual y ha crecido en ella pelo negro, se ha curado. La persona es pura, y el sacerdote la declarará pura.
es.R: Pero puede que el sacerdote vea que la zona que pica sigue igual y que le ha crecido pelo negro. Entonces se ha curado. La persona es pura, y el sacerdote tiene que decirlo.

fr.L: Mais si à ses yeux la teigne s’est maintenue, et [si] du poil noir y a poussé, la teigne est guérie ; il [est] pur ; et le prêtre le déclarera pur.
fr.B: Mais si, de l’avis du prêtre, la dartre n’a pas changé et que des poils noirs y ont poussé, elle est guérie. La personne est pure, et le prêtre la déclarera pure.
fr.R: Mais le prêtre peut voir que la plaque qui démange est restée la même et que des poils noirs y ont poussé. Alors elle est guérie. La personne est pure, et le prêtre doit le dire.

sw.L: Lakini choa ikiwa imesimama machoni pake, na nywele nyeusi zimeota ndani yake, choa imepona; yeye [ni] safi; na kuhani atamtangaza kuwa safi.
sw.B: Lakini kwa maoni ya kuhani choa ikiwa haijabadilika, na nywele nyeusi zimeota ndani yake, imepona. Mtu huyo ni safi, na kuhani atamtangaza kuwa safi.
sw.R: Lakini huenda kuhani akaona kwamba sehemu inayowasha imebaki vilevile, na nywele nyeusi zimeota ndani yake. Basi imepona. Mtu huyo ni safi, na lazima kuhani aseme hivyo.

decisions.choice: black hair has sprouted: healthy hair growing back
decisions.reason: The verb is used of plants springing up (Genesis 2:5). New dark hair shows that the skin is healthy again.

decisions.choice: in his eyes: in the priest's judgment
decisions.reason: See verse 5.

source.text: וְאִישׁ֙ אֽוֹ־אִשָּׁ֔ה כִּֽי־יִהְיֶ֥ה בְעוֹר־בְּשָׂרָ֖ם בֶּהָרֹ֑ת בֶּהָרֹ֖ת לְבָנֹֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And [a] man or [a] woman, when will be in [the] skin of their flesh bright spots, bright spots white,

en.L: And a man or a woman, when there are in the skin of their flesh bright spots, white bright spots,
en.B: When a man or a woman has bright spots on the skin, white bright spots,
en.R: A man or a woman may have shiny spots on their skin, white shiny spots.

es.L: Y un hombre o una mujer, cuando haya en la piel de su carne manchas brillantes, manchas brillantes blancas,
es.B: Cuando un hombre o una mujer tenga manchas brillantes en la piel, manchas brillantes blancas,
es.R: Un hombre o una mujer puede tener manchas que brillan en la piel, manchas blancas que brillan.

fr.L: Et un homme ou une femme, lorsqu’il y aura sur la peau de leur chair des taches brillantes, des taches brillantes blanches,
fr.B: Lorsqu’un homme ou une femme a sur la peau des taches brillantes, des taches brillantes blanches,
fr.R: Un homme ou une femme peut avoir sur la peau des taches qui brillent, des taches blanches qui brillent.

sw.L: Na mwanamume au mwanamke, watakapokuwa na madoa yanayong'aa katika ngozi ya miili yao, madoa meupe yanayong'aa,
sw.B: Mwanamume au mwanamke akiwa na madoa yanayong'aa kwenye ngozi, madoa meupe yanayong'aa,
sw.R: Mwanamume au mwanamke anaweza kuwa na madoa yanayong'aa kwenye ngozi yake, madoa meupe yanayong'aa.

decisions.choice: bright spots, white bright spots: the repetition stresses them
decisions.reason: The repeated word describes several spots, all of them white. Again the law names a man or a woman (verse 29).

source.text: וְרָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֧ה בְעוֹר־בְּשָׂרָ֛ם בֶּהָרֹ֖ת כֵּה֣וֹת לְבָנֹ֑ת בֹּ֥הַק ה֛וּא פָּרַ֥ח בָּע֖וֹר טָה֥וֹר הֽוּא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: and will see the priest, and there! in [the] skin of their flesh [are] bright spots faint white; [a] rash it [is]; it has broken out in the skin; clean he [is].

en.L: and the priest looks, and there! in the skin of their flesh [are] faint white bright spots; it [is] a rash; it has broken out in the skin; he [is] clean.
en.B: and the priest finds that the spots on their skin are a dull white, it is a rash, nothing more, breaking out on the skin. The person is clean.
en.R: The priest must look at them. If the spots are a pale white, it is only a rash that does no harm. It has broken out on the skin, but the person is clean.

es.L: y el sacerdote mira, y he aquí, en la piel de su carne [hay] manchas brillantes de un blanco apagado; sarpullido [es]; ha brotado en la piel; puro [es].
es.B: y el sacerdote ve que las manchas de su piel son de un blanco apagado, es un sarpullido y nada más, que ha brotado en la piel. La persona es pura.
es.R: El sacerdote tiene que mirarlas. Si las manchas son de un blanco pálido, es solo un sarpullido que no hace daño. Ha brotado en la piel, pero la persona es pura.

fr.L: et [si] le prêtre regarde, et voici, sur la peau de leur chair [il y a] des taches brillantes d’un blanc terne ; c’[est] une éruption ; elle a éclaté sur la peau ; il [est] pur.
fr.B: et que le prêtre constate que les taches de la peau sont d’un blanc terne, c’est une simple éruption qui s’est déclarée sur la peau. La personne est pure.
fr.R: Le prêtre doit les regarder. Si les taches sont d’un blanc pâle, ce n’est qu’une éruption sans danger. Elle s’est déclarée sur la peau, mais la personne est pure.

sw.L: na kuhani akiangalia, na tazama, katika ngozi ya miili yao [kuna] madoa yanayong'aa meupe yaliyofifia; ni upele; umechipuka katika ngozi; yeye [ni] safi.
sw.B: na kuhani akiona kwamba madoa ya ngozi yao ni meupe yaliyofifia, ni upele tu uliochipuka katika ngozi. Mtu huyo ni safi.
sw.R: Lazima kuhani ayaangalie. Ikiwa madoa ni meupe yaliyopauka, ni upele tu usio na madhara. Umechipuka kwenye ngozi, lakini mtu huyo ni safi.

decisions.choice: rash: a pale, harmless spotting of the skin
decisions.reason: The word appears only here. It names white spots on the skin that do not make a person unclean, perhaps a condition in which the skin loses its color in patches. The dull white shows that it is not the disease.

decisions.choice: nothing more / that does no harm
decisions.reason: The verse ends 'he is clean'. Balanced and Readable make clear that the rash is harmless.

decisions.choice: "sarpullido"
decisions.reason: An everyday word for a harmless rash, kept apart from "erupción escamosa", the scall of verse 30.

decisions.choice: "une éruption" (L); "une simple éruption" (B); "une éruption sans danger" (R)
decisions.reason: An ordinary word for a rash, kept apart from "dartre", the scall of verse 30.

decisions.choice: "upele"
decisions.reason: The everyday word for a rash, kept apart from "choa", the scall of verse 30.

source.text: וְאִ֕ישׁ כִּ֥י יִמָּרֵ֖ט רֹאשׁ֑וֹ קֵרֵ֥חַ ה֖וּא טָה֥וֹר הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And [a] man, when becomes bare his head, bald he [is]; clean he [is].

en.L: And a man, when [the hair of] his head falls out, he [is] bald; he [is] clean.
en.B: When a man loses the hair of his head, he is bald, but he is clean.
en.R: A man may lose the hair on his head. He is bald, but he is clean.

es.L: Y un hombre, cuando se le cae [el pelo de] la cabeza, calvo [es]; puro [es].
es.B: Cuando a un hombre se le cae el pelo de la cabeza, es calvo, pero es puro.
es.R: Un hombre puede perder el pelo de la cabeza. Es calvo, pero es puro.

fr.L: Et un homme, lorsque [les cheveux de] sa tête tombent, il [est] chauve ; il [est] pur.
fr.B: Lorsqu’un homme perd les cheveux de sa tête, il est chauve, mais il est pur.
fr.R: Un homme peut perdre ses cheveux. Il est chauve, mais il est pur.

sw.L: Na mwanamume, [nywele za] kichwa chake zitakapopukutika, ana upara; yeye [ni] safi.
sw.B: Nywele za kichwa cha mwanamume zikipukutika, ana upara, lakini ni safi.
sw.R: Mwanamume anaweza kupoteza nywele za kichwa chake. Ana upara, lakini ni safi.

decisions.choice: bald: losing hair is not the disease
decisions.reason: Since hair is a sign in these laws (verses 3, 30), the law makes clear that ordinary baldness, on the top or back of the head (here) or at the front (verse 41), does not make a man unclean. Only a mark of the disease on the bald skin does (verses 42-44). These verses speak of a man; verses 29 and 38 named a man or a woman.

decisions.choice: becomes bare: the hair falls out
decisions.reason: The verb means to make smooth or bare, here of a head losing its hair.

decisions.choice: [the hair of] his head falls out
decisions.reason: Literal supplies 'the hair of' in brackets, since 'his head becomes bare' would be unclear.

source.text: וְאִם֙ מִפְּאַ֣ת פָּנָ֔יו יִמָּרֵ֖ט רֹאשׁ֑וֹ גִּבֵּ֥חַ ה֖וּא טָה֥וֹר הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And if from [the] edge of his face becomes bare his head, bald at the forehead he [is]; clean he [is].

en.L: And if [the hair of] his head falls out from the edge of his face, he [is] bald at the forehead; he [is] clean.
en.B: If he loses the hair at the front of his head, he is bald at the forehead, but he is clean.
en.R: Or he may lose the hair at the front of his head. He is bald there, but he is clean.

es.L: Y si desde el borde de su rostro se le cae [el pelo de] la cabeza, calvo de la frente [es]; puro [es].
es.B: Si pierde el pelo de la parte delantera de la cabeza, es calvo de la frente, pero es puro.
es.R: O puede perder el pelo de la parte de delante de la cabeza. Allí es calvo, pero es puro.

fr.L: Et si [les cheveux de] sa tête tombent du côté de son visage, il [est] chauve du front ; il [est] pur.
fr.B: S’il perd les cheveux du devant de la tête, il a le front dégarni, mais il est pur.
fr.R: Ou il peut perdre les cheveux sur le devant de la tête. Il est chauve à cet endroit, mais il est pur.

sw.L: Na ikiwa [nywele za] kichwa chake zitapukutika kutoka upande wa uso wake, ana upara wa paji; yeye [ni] safi.
sw.B: Akipoteza nywele za mbele ya kichwa chake, ana upara wa mbele, lakini ni safi.
sw.R: Au anaweza kupoteza nywele za mbele ya kichwa. Ana upara hapo, lakini ni safi.

decisions.choice: from the edge of his face, bald at the forehead: a receding hairline
decisions.reason: Two different words name baldness on the crown or back of the head (verse 40) and at the front (here). Verses 42-43 use both.

source.text: וְכִֽי־יִהְיֶ֤ה בַקָּרַ֨חַת֙ א֣וֹ בַגַּבַּ֔חַת נֶ֖גַע לָבָ֣ן אֲדַמְדָּ֑ם צָרַ֤עַת פֹּרַ֨חַת֙ הִ֔וא בְּקָרַחְתּ֖וֹ א֥וֹ בְגַבַּחְתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And when will be on the bald head or on the bald forehead [a] mark white reddish, scale disease breaking out it [is] on his bald head or on his bald forehead.

en.L: But when there is on the bald head or on the bald forehead a reddish-white mark, it [is] scale disease breaking out on his bald head or on his bald forehead.
en.B: But if a reddish-white sore appears on his bald head or forehead, it is a serious skin disease breaking out on his bald head or forehead.
en.R: But a pinkish-white sore may appear on the bald place, at the back or the front. Then a serious skin disease is breaking out there.

es.L: Pero cuando haya en la calva o en la calva de la frente una marca blanca rojiza, enfermedad de la piel que brota [es] en su calva o en su calva de la frente.
es.B: Pero si aparece una llaga de color blanco rojizo en su calva o en su frente calva, es una enfermedad grave de la piel que brota en su calva o en su frente.
es.R: Pero puede aparecer una llaga de color blanco rosado en la parte calva, atrás o adelante. Entonces está brotando allí una enfermedad grave de la piel.

fr.L: Mais lorsqu’il y aura sur le crâne chauve ou sur le front chauve une marque d’un blanc rougeâtre, c’[est] une maladie de peau qui éclate sur son crâne chauve ou sur son front chauve.
fr.B: Mais si une lésion d’un blanc rougeâtre apparaît sur son crâne chauve ou sur son front dégarni, c’est une maladie de peau grave qui se déclare sur son crâne ou sur son front.
fr.R: Mais une plaie d’un blanc rosé peut apparaître sur la partie chauve, derrière ou devant. Alors une maladie de peau grave est en train de se déclarer à cet endroit.

sw.L: Lakini kukiwa na alama nyeupe yenye wekundu kwenye upara wa kichwa au kwenye upara wa paji, ni ugonjwa wa ngozi unaochipuka kwenye upara wake wa kichwa au kwenye upara wake wa paji.
sw.B: Lakini kidonda cheupe chenye wekundu kikitokea kwenye upara wake wa kichwa au wa paji, ni ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi unaochipuka kwenye upara wake wa kichwa au wa paji.
sw.R: Lakini kidonda cheupe chenye rangi ya waridi kinaweza kutokea mahali penye upara, nyuma au mbele. Basi ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi unachipuka hapo.

decisions.choice: reddish-white mark: the color of an active mark
decisions.reason: As in verses 19 and 24. On bare scalp there is no hair to show the signs, so the color and the swelling (verse 43) are what the priest looks for.

source.text: וְרָאָ֨ה אֹת֜וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה שְׂאֵת־הַנֶּ֨גַע֙ לְבָנָ֣ה אֲדַמְדֶּ֔מֶת בְּקָרַחְתּ֖וֹ א֣וֹ בְגַבַּחְתּ֑וֹ כְּמַרְאֵ֥ה צָרַ֖עַת ע֥וֹר בָּשָֽׂר׃

records.literal_gloss: And will see him the priest, and there! [the] swelling of the mark [is] white reddish on his bald head or on his bald forehead, like [the] appearance of scale disease of [the] skin of flesh,

en.L: And the priest shall look at him, and there! the swelling of the mark [is] reddish-white on his bald head or on his bald forehead, like the appearance of scale disease of the skin of the flesh;
en.B: The priest is to examine him. If the swollen sore on his bald head or forehead is reddish-white, looking like a serious skin disease on the body,
en.R: The priest must look at him. The swollen sore on his bald head may be pinkish-white. It may look like serious skin disease does on other parts of the body.

es.L: Y el sacerdote lo mirará, y he aquí, la hinchazón de la marca [es] blanca rojiza en su calva o en su calva de la frente, como el aspecto de la enfermedad de la piel de la piel de la carne;
es.B: El sacerdote lo examinará. Si la llaga hinchada en su calva o en su frente es de color blanco rojizo, con el aspecto de una enfermedad grave de la piel del cuerpo,
es.R: El sacerdote tiene que mirarlo. Puede que la llaga hinchada en su calva sea de color blanco rosado. Puede que se parezca a una enfermedad grave de la piel en otras partes del cuerpo.

fr.L: Et le prêtre le regardera, et voici, l’enflure de la marque [est] d’un blanc rougeâtre sur son crâne chauve ou sur son front chauve, comme l’aspect de la maladie de peau de la peau de la chair ;
fr.B: Le prêtre l’examinera. Si la lésion enflée sur son crâne ou son front dégarni est d’un blanc rougeâtre, et ressemble à une maladie de peau grave sur le corps,
fr.R: Le prêtre doit le regarder. La plaie enflée sur sa tête chauve est peut-être d’un blanc rosé. Elle ressemble peut-être à une maladie de peau grave sur d’autres parties du corps.

sw.L: Na kuhani atamwangalia, na tazama, uvimbe wa alama [ni] mweupe wenye wekundu kwenye upara wake wa kichwa au kwenye upara wake wa paji, kama sura ya ugonjwa wa ngozi wa ngozi ya mwili;
sw.B: Kuhani atamchunguza. Ikiwa kidonda kilichovimba kwenye upara wake wa kichwa au wa paji ni cheupe chenye wekundu, kinachoonekana kama ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi mwilini,
sw.R: Lazima kuhani amwangalie. Huenda kidonda kilichovimba kwenye upara wake ni cheupe chenye rangi ya waridi. Huenda kinaonekana kama ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi unavyoonekana kwenye sehemu nyingine za mwili.

decisions.choice: like scale disease of the skin: judged by the signs of verses 2-28
decisions.reason: The bald scalp is treated as bare skin, not as a place where hair grows (verses 29-37).

source.text: אִישׁ־צָר֥וּעַ ה֖וּא טָמֵ֣א ה֑וּא טַמֵּ֧א יְטַמְּאֶ֛נּוּ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן בְּרֹאשׁ֥וֹ נִגְעֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: [a] man with scale disease he [is]; unclean he [is]; surely will pronounce him unclean the priest; on his head [is] his mark.

en.L: he [is] a man with scale disease; he [is] unclean; the priest shall surely pronounce him unclean; his mark [is] on his head.
en.B: he is a man with a serious skin disease and he is unclean. The priest must declare him unclean; the sore is on his head.
en.R: Then the man has a serious skin disease and is unclean. The priest must say that he is unclean. The sore is on his head.

es.L: hombre con enfermedad de la piel [es]; impuro [es]; el sacerdote ciertamente lo declarará impuro; en su cabeza [está] su marca.
es.B: es un hombre con una enfermedad grave de la piel, y es impuro. El sacerdote tiene que declararlo impuro; la llaga está en su cabeza.
es.R: Entonces el hombre tiene una enfermedad grave de la piel y es impuro. El sacerdote tiene que decir que es impuro. La llaga está en su cabeza.

fr.L: c’[est] un homme atteint de maladie de peau ; il [est] impur ; le prêtre le déclarera assurément impur ; sa marque [est] sur sa tête.
fr.B: c’est un homme atteint d’une maladie de peau grave, et il est impur. Le prêtre doit le déclarer impur ; la lésion est sur sa tête.
fr.R: Alors l’homme a une maladie de peau grave et il est impur. Le prêtre doit dire qu’il est impur. La plaie est sur sa tête.

sw.L: yeye [ni] mtu mwenye ugonjwa wa ngozi; yeye [ni] najisi; kuhani hakika atamtangaza kuwa najisi; alama yake [iko] kichwani mwake.
sw.B: yeye ni mtu mwenye ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi, naye ni najisi. Lazima kuhani amtangaze kuwa najisi; kidonda kiko kichwani mwake.
sw.R: Basi mwanamume huyo ana ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi, naye ni najisi. Lazima kuhani aseme kwamba yeye ni najisi. Kidonda kiko kichwani mwake.

decisions.choice: surely pronounce unclean: the verb is doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: There is no doubt, and no week of waiting.

decisions.choice: a man with scale disease: the word names the person by the disease
decisions.reason: This word is used again in verse 45. Since the case is that of a bald man (verse 40), no wording for both men and women is used here.

source.text: וְהַצָּר֜וּעַ אֲשֶׁר־בּ֣וֹ הַנֶּ֗גַע בְּגָדָ֞יו יִהְי֤וּ פְרֻמִים֙ וְרֹאשׁוֹ֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה פָר֔וּעַ וְעַל־שָׂפָ֖ם יַעְטֶ֑ה וְטָמֵ֥א׀טָמֵ֖א יִקְרָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And the [one with] scale disease who [has] on him the mark, his garments will be torn, and his head will be let loose, and over [the] upper lip he will cover, and 'Unclean! Unclean!' he will call out.

en.L: And the one with scale disease, on whom the mark [is], his garments shall be torn, and his head shall be let loose, and he shall cover over [his] upper lip, and 'Unclean! Unclean!' he shall call out.
en.B: The person who has the sore of serious skin disease is to go about in torn clothes, with the hair of the head left loose. They are to cover their upper lip and shout, 'Unclean, unclean!'
en.R: Anyone who has this disease must dress in torn clothes and leave their hair loose and uncombed. They must cover their upper lip. They must shout, 'Unclean, unclean!'

es.L: Y el que tiene la enfermedad de la piel, en quien [está] la marca, sus vestidos estarán rasgados, y [el pelo de] su cabeza estará suelto, y se cubrirá [el] labio superior, y gritará: “¡Impuro! ¡Impuro!”.
es.B: La persona que tenga la llaga de una enfermedad grave de la piel andará con la ropa rasgada y con el pelo suelto. Se cubrirá el labio superior y gritará: “¡Impuro, impuro!”.
es.R: Quien tenga esta enfermedad tiene que vestir ropa rasgada y llevar el pelo suelto y sin peinar. Tiene que cubrirse el labio superior. Tiene que gritar: “¡Impuro, impuro!”.

fr.L: Et celui qui a la maladie de peau, sur qui [est] la marque, ses vêtements seront déchirés, et [les cheveux de] sa tête seront dénoués, et il se couvrira la lèvre supérieure, et il criera : “Impur ! Impur !”
fr.B: La personne qui a la lésion d’une maladie de peau grave portera des vêtements déchirés et laissera ses cheveux dénoués. Elle se couvrira la lèvre supérieure et criera : “Impur, impur !”
fr.R: Toute personne qui a cette maladie doit porter des vêtements déchirés et laisser ses cheveux en désordre, sans les coiffer. Elle doit se couvrir la lèvre supérieure. Elle doit crier : “Impur, impur !”

sw.L: Na mwenye ugonjwa wa ngozi, ambaye alama [iko] juu yake, nguo zake zitakuwa zimeraruliwa, na [nywele za] kichwa chake zitaachwa bila kufungwa, naye atafunika mdomo wake wa juu, naye atapiga kelele, 'Najisi! Najisi!'
sw.B: Mtu mwenye kidonda cha ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi atavaa nguo zilizoraruka, na nywele za kichwa chake ataziacha timtim. Atafunika mdomo wake wa juu na kupiga kelele, 'Najisi, najisi!'
sw.R: Mtu yeyote mwenye ugonjwa huu lazima avae nguo zilizoraruka na kuziacha nywele zake timtim bila kuzichana. Lazima afunike mdomo wake wa juu. Lazima apige kelele, 'Najisi, najisi!'

decisions.choice: torn clothes and loose hair: the signs of mourning
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes and leaving the hair unbound are what mourners did (Genesis 37:34; compare 10:6 and 21:10, where priests are told not to do them). The person with the disease bears the outward marks of grief, as one cut off from the life of the camp. 'Let loose' may mean unbound or uncombed; either way the hair is left in disorder.

decisions.choice: cover the upper lip: another sign of grief or shame
decisions.reason: Covering the upper lip or moustache is done in mourning or shame in Ezekiel 24:17, 22 and Micah 3:7.

decisions.choice: 'Unclean, unclean!': a warning to others
decisions.reason: The person calls out so that others will not come near and touch them, since uncleanness passes by touch (5:3). Lamentations 4:15 echoes the cry, shouted at those driven out of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the person / anyone / they
decisions.reason: The law is for men and women with the disease, so Balanced and Readable use 'they' where the Hebrew says 'he'. Readable gives the sense of 'let loose' as 'loose and uncombed'. The cry is in single quotation marks because it stands inside the LORD's speech.

decisions.choice: “¡Impuro, impuro!” in the masculine at every level
decisions.reason: The cry is a fixed warning, given in the Hebrew in the masculine form used for any person in these laws. Spanish keeps it as one formula rather than making it vary with the speaker; a woman with the disease would naturally say "impura".

decisions.choice: “Impur, impur !” in the masculine at every level
decisions.reason: The cry is a fixed warning, given in the Hebrew in the masculine form used for any person in these laws. French keeps it as one formula rather than making it vary with the speaker; a woman with the disease would naturally say "impure".

source.text: כָּל־יְמֵ֞י אֲשֶׁ֨ר הַנֶּ֥גַע בּ֛וֹ יִטְמָ֖א טָמֵ֣א ה֑וּא בָּדָ֣ד יֵשֵׁ֔ב מִח֥וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה מוֹשָׁבֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: All [the] days that the mark [is] on him he will be unclean; unclean he [is]; alone he will dwell; outside of the camp [is] his dwelling.

en.L: All the days that the mark [is] on him he shall be unclean; he [is] unclean; he shall dwell alone; outside the camp [shall be] his dwelling.
en.B: For the whole time the sore is on them they are unclean. Being unclean, they are to live by themselves, making their home outside the camp.
en.R: The person will be unclean for as long as the sore is on them. Because they are unclean, they must stay by themselves. They must have their home outside the camp.

es.L: Todos los días que la marca [esté] en él será impuro; impuro [es]; habitará solo; fuera del campamento [será] su morada.
es.B: Durante todo el tiempo que tenga la llaga será impura. Por ser impura, vivirá aparte, y tendrá su vivienda fuera del campamento.
es.R: La persona será impura mientras tenga la llaga. Como es impura, tiene que vivir aparte. Tiene que tener su casa fuera del campamento.

fr.L: Tous les jours où la marque [sera] sur lui, il sera impur ; il [est] impur ; il habitera seul ; hors du camp [sera] sa demeure.
fr.B: Aussi longtemps que la lésion sera sur elle, la personne sera impure. Étant impure, elle vivra à part et aura sa demeure hors du camp.
fr.R: La personne sera impure tant qu’elle aura la plaie. Parce qu’elle est impure, elle doit rester à l’écart. Elle doit avoir sa maison hors du camp.

sw.L: Siku zote ambazo alama [iko] juu yake atakuwa najisi; yeye [ni] najisi; atakaa peke yake; nje ya kambi [patakuwa] makao yake.
sw.B: Muda wote kidonda kikiwa juu yake atakuwa najisi. Kwa kuwa ni najisi, ataishi peke yake, na makao yake yatakuwa nje ya kambi.
sw.R: Mtu huyo atakuwa najisi muda wote kidonda kikiwa juu yake. Kwa sababu ni najisi, lazima akae peke yake. Lazima nyumba yake iwe nje ya kambi.

decisions.choice: alone, outside the camp: separated from the community
decisions.reason: The camp was where God's dwelling stood among the people, and Numbers 5:2-3 gives the reason for sending the unclean out: the camp, where God lives among them, must not be made unclean. Living outside it, the person could not come to the sanctuary or share in the common life until healed and cleansed (14:1-8). Numbers 12:14-15 (Miriam) and 2 Kings 7:3 (four men at the city gate) show the rule in practice. 'Alone' means apart from the clean; such people could live together, as the four men did.

decisions.choice: he shall be unclean; he is unclean: the state lasts as long as the mark
decisions.reason: The repetition stresses that the uncleanness does not end until the mark is gone.

source.text: וְהַבֶּ֕גֶד כִּֽי־יִהְיֶ֥ה ב֖וֹ נֶ֣גַע צָרָ֑עַת בְּבֶ֣גֶד צֶ֔מֶר א֖וֹ בְּבֶ֥גֶד פִּשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And the garment, when will be in it [a] mark of scale disease, in [a] garment of wool or in [a] garment of linen,

en.L: And the garment, when there is in it a mark of scale disease, in a garment of wool or in a garment of linen,
en.B: When a patch of mold is found in clothing, whether wool or linen clothing,
en.R: Mold may get into clothing made of wool or linen.

es.L: Y el vestido, cuando haya en él marca de enfermedad de la piel, en un vestido de lana o en un vestido de lino,
es.B: Cuando se encuentre una mancha de moho en la ropa, sea ropa de lana o de lino,
es.R: Puede que salga moho en la ropa de lana o de lino.

fr.L: Et le vêtement, lorsqu’il y aura en lui une marque de maladie de peau, dans un vêtement de laine ou dans un vêtement de lin,
fr.B: Lorsqu’une tache de moisissure se trouve sur un vêtement, qu’il soit de laine ou de lin,
fr.R: Il peut y avoir de la moisissure sur des vêtements de laine ou de lin.

sw.L: Na vazi, litakapokuwa na alama ya ugonjwa wa ngozi ndani yake, katika vazi la sufu au katika vazi la kitani,
sw.B: Doa la ukungu likionekana katika nguo, iwe nguo ya sufu au ya kitani,
sw.R: Ukungu unaweza kuingia katika nguo za sufu au za kitani.

decisions.choice: a mark of scale disease in a garment: a spreading growth such as mold or mildew
decisions.reason: The same term used for the disease of the skin is used for a growth in cloth and leather, and in the walls of a house (14:34). It cannot be the same illness. It is a blight that spreads and eats into the material, such as mold or mildew, with greenish or reddish patches (verse 49). Like the disease in people it makes a thing unclean, and the priest examines it and rules in the same way, with weeks of waiting.

decisions.choice: wool or linen: the two common cloths
decisions.reason: Israel's clothing was mostly wool from sheep or linen from flax (Deuteronomy 22:11).

decisions.choice: a patch of mold / mold
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say 'mold' for the growth in cloth, as in 14:34, and 'patch' for the mark. Literal keeps 'mark of scale disease', so that a reader can see the Hebrew uses the same words as for the skin.

decisions.choice: "marca de enfermedad de la piel" (L); "mancha de moho", "moho" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the words used for the skin, odd as "enfermedad de la piel" is for cloth, so that a reader sees that the Hebrew uses the same term. Balanced and Readable say "moho" for the growth and "mancha" for the mark, as the English says "mold" and "patch".

decisions.choice: "marque de maladie de peau" (L); "tache de moisissure", "moisissure" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the words used for the skin, odd as "maladie de peau" is for cloth, so that a reader sees that the Hebrew uses the same term. Balanced and Readable say "moisissure" for the growth and "tache" for the mark, as the English says "mold" and "patch".

decisions.choice: "alama ya ugonjwa wa ngozi" (L); "doa la ukungu", "ukungu" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the words used for the skin, odd as "ugonjwa wa ngozi" is for cloth, so that a reader sees that the Hebrew uses the same term. Balanced and Readable say "ukungu", mold or mildew, for the growth and "doa" for the mark, as the English says "mold" and "patch".

source.text: א֤וֹ בִֽשְׁתִי֙ א֣וֹ בְעֵ֔רֶב לַפִּשְׁתִּ֖ים וְלַצָּ֑מֶר א֣וֹ בְע֔וֹר א֖וֹ בְּכָל־מְלֶ֥אכֶת עֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: or in [the] warp or in [the] woof of the linen or of the wool, or in [a] hide or in any work of hide,

en.L: or in the warp or in the woof of the linen or of the wool, or in a hide or in any work of hide,
en.B: or in the warp or the weft of linen or wool, or in leather or anything made of leather,
en.R: It may be in the lengthwise or crosswise threads of linen or wool cloth, or in leather or anything made of leather.

es.L: o en la urdimbre o en la trama del lino o de la lana, o en una piel o en cualquier obra de piel,
es.B: o en la urdimbre o la trama de lino o de lana, o en cuero o en cualquier cosa hecha de cuero,
es.R: Puede estar en los hilos a lo largo o a lo ancho de la tela de lino o de lana, o en cuero o en cualquier cosa hecha de cuero.

fr.L: ou dans la chaîne ou dans la trame du lin ou de la laine, ou dans une peau ou dans tout ouvrage de peau,
fr.B: ou dans la chaîne ou la trame de lin ou de laine, ou dans du cuir ou tout objet de cuir,
fr.R: Elle peut être dans les fils en long ou en travers d’un tissu de lin ou de laine, ou dans du cuir ou n’importe quel objet en cuir.

sw.L: au katika mtande au katika mshindio wa kitani au wa sufu, au katika ngozi au katika kazi yoyote ya ngozi,
sw.B: au katika mtande au mshindio wa kitani au wa sufu, au katika ngozi au kitu chochote kilichotengenezwa kwa ngozi,
sw.R: Unaweza kuwa katika nyuzi za urefu au za upana za kitambaa cha kitani au cha sufu, au katika ngozi au kitu chochote kilichotengenezwa kwa ngozi.

decisions.choice: warp and woof: the threads of a weave, or yarn for weaving
alternatives: yarn for the warp or the woof
decisions.reason: The warp is the set of threads running lengthwise on a loom, and the woof the threads woven across them. Since a mark can be in one and not the other, and can be torn out of either (verse 56), the words may mean yarn spun for the warp or the woof and not yet woven, or simply two kinds of woven or knitted material. The sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: hide, work of hide: leather and things made of leather
decisions.reason: Leather was used for clothing, bags, water skins and tent covers.

decisions.choice: warp or weft / lengthwise or crosswise threads; leather
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the old pair 'warp and woof'. Balanced uses the modern 'weft', and Readable says what the two words mean. Balanced and Readable say 'leather' for hide.

decisions.choice: "la urdimbre o la trama" (L, B); "los hilos a lo largo o a lo ancho" (R); "piel" (L), "cuero" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Urdimbre" and "trama" are the ordinary Spanish weaving terms for the two sets of threads. Readable says what they are, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "la chaîne ou la trame" (L, B); "les fils en long ou en travers" (R); "peau" (L), "cuir" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Chaîne" and "trame" are the ordinary French weaving terms for the two sets of threads, so Literal and Balanced share them. Readable says what they are, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "mtande au mshindio" (L, B); "nyuzi za urefu au za upana" (R)
decisions.reason: "Mtande" and "mshindio" are the Swahili weaving terms for the warp and the weft. They are not everyday words, so Readable says what they are, as the English does. "Ngozi" covers both hide and leather.

source.text: וְהָיָ֨ה הַנֶּ֜גַע יְרַקְרַ֣ק׀א֣וֹ אֲדַמְדָּ֗ם בַּבֶּגֶד֩ א֨וֹ בָע֜וֹר אֽוֹ־בַשְּׁתִ֤י אוֹ־בָעֵ֨רֶב֙ א֣וֹ בְכָל־כְּלִי־ע֔וֹר נֶ֥גַע צָרַ֖עַת ה֑וּא וְהָרְאָ֖ה אֶת־הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: and is the mark greenish or reddish in the garment or in the hide or in the warp or in the woof or in any article of hide, [a] mark of scale disease it [is], and it will be shown to the priest.

en.L: and the mark is greenish or reddish in the garment or in the hide or in the warp or in the woof or in any article of hide, it [is] a mark of scale disease, and it shall be shown to the priest.
en.B: and the patch in the clothing or leather, in the warp or weft, or in any leather article is greenish or reddish, it is a patch of mold and must be shown to the priest.
en.R: If the patch in the cloth, the threads or the leather is greenish or reddish, it is mold. It must be shown to the priest.

es.L: y la marca es verdosa o rojiza en el vestido o en la piel o en la urdimbre o en la trama o en cualquier objeto de piel, marca de enfermedad de la piel [es], y será mostrada al sacerdote.
es.B: y la mancha en la ropa o el cuero, en la urdimbre o la trama, o en cualquier objeto de cuero es verdosa o rojiza, es una mancha de moho y se mostrará al sacerdote.
es.R: Si la mancha en la tela, en los hilos o en el cuero es verdosa o rojiza, es moho. Hay que mostrarla al sacerdote.

fr.L: et [si] la marque est verdâtre ou rougeâtre dans le vêtement ou dans la peau ou dans la chaîne ou dans la trame ou dans tout objet de peau, c’[est] une marque de maladie de peau, et elle sera montrée au prêtre.
fr.B: et que la tache sur le vêtement ou le cuir, dans la chaîne ou la trame, ou sur un objet de cuir est verdâtre ou rougeâtre, c’est une tache de moisissure, et elle sera montrée au prêtre.
fr.R: Si la tache sur le tissu, les fils ou le cuir est verdâtre ou rougeâtre, c’est de la moisissure. Il faut la montrer au prêtre.

sw.L: na alama ikawa ya kijanikijani au ya wekundu katika vazi au katika ngozi au katika mtande au katika mshindio au katika kitu chochote cha ngozi, ni alama ya ugonjwa wa ngozi, nayo itaonyeshwa kwa kuhani.
sw.B: na doa katika nguo au ngozi, katika mtande au mshindio, au katika kitu chochote cha ngozi likawa la kijanikijani au la wekundu, ni doa la ukungu, nalo litaonyeshwa kwa kuhani.
sw.R: Ikiwa doa katika kitambaa, nyuzi au ngozi ni la kijanikijani au la wekundu, ni ukungu. Lazima lionyeshwe kwa kuhani.

decisions.choice: greenish or reddish: tinged with green or red
decisions.reason: As in 14:37, the doubled syllables make the colors faint. The word for 'green' is used of plants and can include a yellowish green.

decisions.choice: it is a mark of scale disease: it is to be treated as one
decisions.reason: The patch is taken to be the blight until the priest has examined it, so it must be shown to him.

source.text: וְרָאָ֥ה הַכֹּהֵ֖ן אֶת־הַנָּ֑גַע וְהִסְגִּ֥יר אֶת־הַנֶּ֖גַע שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And will see the priest the mark and will shut up the mark seven days.

en.L: And the priest shall look at the mark and shut up the [thing with the] mark seven days.
en.B: The priest is to examine the patch and shut the article away for seven days.
en.R: The priest must look at the mold. Then he must put the thing away for seven days.

es.L: Y el sacerdote mirará la marca y encerrará [lo que tiene] la marca siete días.
es.B: El sacerdote examinará la mancha y aislará el objeto durante siete días.
es.R: El sacerdote tiene que mirar el moho. Luego tiene que guardar la cosa aparte durante siete días.

fr.L: Et le prêtre regardera la marque et enfermera [ce qui a] la marque sept jours.
fr.B: Le prêtre examinera la tache et mettra l’objet à l’écart pendant sept jours.
fr.R: Le prêtre doit regarder la moisissure. Ensuite, il doit ranger l’objet à part pendant sept jours.

sw.L: Na kuhani ataiangalia alama na kukifungia [kitu chenye] alama siku saba.
sw.B: Kuhani atalichunguza doa na kukitenga kitu hicho kwa siku saba.
sw.R: Lazima kuhani auangalie ukungu. Kisha lazima akiweke kitu hicho mahali pa pekee kwa siku saba.

decisions.choice: shut up the mark: set the article aside for a week
decisions.reason: As a person is shut up (verse 4), so is the thing with the mark. The priest sets it apart to see whether the mark spreads.

decisions.choice: put the thing away
decisions.reason: For an object, Readable says 'put away' where it says 'keep away from others' for a person.

source.text: וְרָאָ֨ה אֶת־הַנֶּ֜גַע בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י כִּֽי־פָשָׂ֤ה הַנֶּ֨גַע֙ בַּ֠בֶּגֶד אֽוֹ־בַשְּׁתִ֤י אֽוֹ־בָעֵ֨רֶב֙ א֣וֹ בָע֔וֹר לְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־יֵעָשֶׂ֥ה הָע֖וֹר לִמְלָאכָ֑ה צָרַ֧עַת מַמְאֶ֛רֶת הַנֶּ֖גַע טָמֵ֥א הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will see the mark on the seventh day; if has spread the mark in the garment or in the warp or in the woof or in the hide, for all that is made [of] the hide for work, [a] malignant scale disease the mark [is]; unclean it [is].

en.L: And he shall look at the mark on the seventh day; if the mark has spread in the garment or in the warp or in the woof or in the hide, whatever the hide is made into for use, the mark [is] a malignant scale disease; it [is] unclean.
en.B: On the seventh day he is to look at the patch. If it has spread in the clothing, the warp or weft, or the leather, whatever the leather is used for, it is a spreading mold, and the article is unclean.
en.R: On the seventh day he must look at it again. The mold may have spread in the cloth, the threads or the leather, whatever the leather is used for. Then it is the kind of mold that keeps growing. The thing is unclean.

es.L: Y mirará la marca el séptimo día; si se ha extendido la marca en el vestido o en la urdimbre o en la trama o en la piel, para todo lo que se hace de la piel para uso, enfermedad de la piel maligna [es] la marca; impura [es].
es.B: El séptimo día examinará la mancha. Si se ha extendido en la ropa, la urdimbre o la trama, o el cuero, sea cual sea el uso del cuero, es un moho que se propaga, y el objeto es impuro.
es.R: El séptimo día tiene que mirarlo otra vez. Puede que el moho se haya extendido en la tela, los hilos o el cuero, sea para lo que sea el cuero. Entonces es la clase de moho que sigue creciendo. La cosa es impura.

fr.L: Et il regardera la marque le septième jour ; si la marque s’est étendue dans le vêtement ou dans la chaîne ou dans la trame ou dans la peau, quel que soit l’ouvrage pour lequel la peau est employée, la marque [est] une maladie de peau maligne ; elle [est] impure.
fr.B: Le septième jour, il examinera la tache. Si elle s’est étendue sur le vêtement, la chaîne ou la trame, ou le cuir, quel que soit l’usage du cuir, c’est une moisissure qui se propage, et l’objet est impur.
fr.R: Le septième jour, il doit la regarder encore. La moisissure s’est peut-être étendue dans le tissu, les fils ou le cuir, quel que soit l’usage du cuir. Alors c’est une moisissure qui continue de grandir. L’objet est impur.

sw.L: Naye ataiangalia alama siku ya saba; ikiwa alama imeenea katika vazi au katika mtande au katika mshindio au katika ngozi, kwa kazi yoyote ambayo ngozi hutengenezwa, alama [ni] ugonjwa wa ngozi unaoharibu; ni najisi.
sw.B: Siku ya saba atalichunguza doa. Ikiwa limeenea katika nguo, mtande au mshindio, au ngozi, iwe ngozi hiyo inatumika kwa kazi gani, ni ukungu unaoenea, na kitu hicho ni najisi.
sw.R: Siku ya saba lazima auangalie tena. Huenda ukungu umeenea katika kitambaa, nyuzi au ngozi, iwe ngozi hiyo inatumika kwa kazi gani. Basi ni aina ya ukungu unaoendelea kukua. Kitu hicho ni najisi.

decisions.choice: malignant: destructive, eating away
decisions.reason: The word appears only here, in verse 52 and in 14:44. It comes from a verb meaning to prick or hurt (Ezekiel 28:24, 'a painful thorn'): a growth that eats away and will not stop.

decisions.choice: spreading mold / the kind of mold that keeps growing
decisions.reason: As in 14:44, Balanced and Readable say what 'malignant' means for mold. Literal keeps 'malignant'.

decisions.choice: "maligna" (L); "un moho que se propaga" (B); "la clase de moho que sigue creciendo" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the English: Literal keeps "maligna" for the rare Hebrew word; Balanced and Readable say what it means for mold. The same words return in verse 52 and 14:44.

decisions.choice: "maligne" (L); "une moisissure qui se propage" (B); "une moisissure qui continue de grandir" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the English: Literal keeps "maligne" for the rare Hebrew word; Balanced and Readable say what it means for mold. The same words return in verse 52 and 14:44.

decisions.choice: "unaoharibu" (L); "ukungu unaoenea" (B); "aina ya ukungu unaoendelea kukua" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal says "unaoharibu", destroying, for the rare Hebrew word, which means eating away; Balanced and Readable say what it means for mold, as the English does. The same words return in verse 52 and 14:44.

source.text: וְשָׂרַ֨ף אֶת־הַבֶּ֜גֶד א֥וֹ אֶֽת־הַשְּׁתִ֣י׀א֣וֹ אֶת־הָעֵ֗רֶב בַּצֶּ֨מֶר֙ א֣וֹ בַפִּשְׁתִּ֔ים א֚וֹ אֶת־כָּל־כְּלִ֣י הָע֔וֹר אֲשֶׁר־יִהְיֶ֥ה ב֖וֹ הַנָּ֑גַע כִּֽי־צָרַ֤עַת מַמְאֶ֨רֶת֙ הִ֔וא בָּאֵ֖שׁ תִּשָּׂרֵֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will burn the garment or the warp or the woof, in the wool or in the linen, or any article of the hide in which is the mark, for [a] malignant scale disease it [is]; with fire it will be burned.

en.L: And he shall burn the garment or the warp or the woof, in wool or in linen, or any article of hide in which the mark [is], for it [is] a malignant scale disease; it shall be burned with fire.
en.B: He must burn the clothing, the woolen or linen warp or weft, or the leather article that has the patch in it. Because it is a spreading mold, it must be burned up.
en.R: He must burn the cloth, the threads or the leather that has the mold. It is the kind of mold that keeps growing, so it must be burned in a fire.

es.L: Y quemará el vestido o la urdimbre o la trama, de lana o de lino, o cualquier objeto de piel en que [esté] la marca, porque enfermedad de la piel maligna [es]; con fuego será quemado.
es.B: Quemará la ropa, la urdimbre o la trama de lana o de lino, o el objeto de cuero que tenga la mancha. Como es un moho que se propaga, tiene que ser quemado por completo.
es.R: Tiene que quemar la tela, los hilos o el cuero que tenga el moho. Es la clase de moho que sigue creciendo, así que hay que quemarlo en el fuego.

fr.L: Et il brûlera le vêtement ou la chaîne ou la trame, de laine ou de lin, ou tout objet de peau dans lequel [est] la marque, car c’[est] une maladie de peau maligne ; il sera brûlé au feu.
fr.B: Il devra brûler le vêtement, la chaîne ou la trame de laine ou de lin, ou l’objet de cuir où se trouve la tache. Comme c’est une moisissure qui se propage, il faut le brûler entièrement.
fr.R: Il doit brûler le tissu, les fils ou le cuir qui a la moisissure. C’est une moisissure qui continue de grandir, alors il faut tout brûler dans le feu.

sw.L: Naye atalichoma vazi au mtande au mshindio, wa sufu au wa kitani, au kitu chochote cha ngozi ambacho alama [iko] ndani yake, kwa maana ni ugonjwa wa ngozi unaoharibu; kitachomwa kwa moto.
sw.B: Lazima achome nguo, mtande au mshindio wa sufu au wa kitani, au kitu cha ngozi chenye doa hilo. Kwa kuwa ni ukungu unaoenea, lazima kiteketezwe kwa moto.
sw.R: Lazima achome kitambaa, nyuzi au ngozi yenye ukungu. Ni aina ya ukungu unaoendelea kukua, kwa hiyo lazima kichomwe motoni.

decisions.choice: burned with fire: destroyed so that the blight goes no further
decisions.reason: Burning destroys the thing and the uncleanness in it. A house with the same blight is torn down (14:45).

source.text: וְאִם֮ יִרְאֶ֣ה הַכֹּהֵן֒ וְהִנֵּה֙ לֹא־פָשָׂ֣ה הַנֶּ֔גַע בַּבֶּ֕גֶד א֥וֹ בַשְּׁתִ֖י א֣וֹ בָעֵ֑רֶב א֖וֹ בְּכָל־כְּלִי־עֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: And if will see the priest, and there! not has spread the mark in the garment or in the warp or in the woof or in any article of hide,

en.L: But if the priest looks, and there! the mark has not spread in the garment or in the warp or in the woof or in any article of hide,
en.B: But if the priest examines it and the patch has not spread in the clothing, the warp or weft, or the leather article,
en.R: But the priest may find that the mold has not spread in the cloth, the threads or the leather.

es.L: Pero si el sacerdote mira, y he aquí, no se ha extendido la marca en el vestido o en la urdimbre o en la trama o en cualquier objeto de piel,
es.B: Pero si el sacerdote lo examina y la mancha no se ha extendido en la ropa, la urdimbre o la trama, o el objeto de cuero,
es.R: Pero puede que el sacerdote vea que el moho no se ha extendido en la tela, los hilos o el cuero.

fr.L: Mais si le prêtre regarde, et voici, la marque ne s’est pas étendue dans le vêtement ou dans la chaîne ou dans la trame ou dans tout objet de peau,
fr.B: Mais si le prêtre l’examine et que la tache ne s’est pas étendue sur le vêtement, la chaîne ou la trame, ou l’objet de cuir,
fr.R: Mais le prêtre peut voir que la moisissure ne s’est pas étendue dans le tissu, les fils ou le cuir.

sw.L: Lakini kuhani akiangalia, na tazama, alama haijaenea katika vazi au katika mtande au katika mshindio au katika kitu chochote cha ngozi,
sw.B: Lakini kuhani akikichunguza na doa halijaenea katika nguo, mtande au mshindio, au kitu cha ngozi,
sw.R: Lakini huenda kuhani akaona kwamba ukungu haujaenea katika kitambaa, nyuzi au ngozi.

decisions.choice: the mark has not spread: the doubtful case
decisions.reason: Verses 53-58 deal with a mark that has not spread in the first week, as verses 4-6 do for a person.

source.text: וְצִוָּה֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְכִ֨בְּס֔וּ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־בּ֖וֹ הַנָּ֑גַע וְהִסְגִּיר֥וֹ שִׁבְעַת־יָמִ֖ים שֵׁנִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: then will command the priest, and they will wash [that] which the mark [is] in, and he will shut it up seven days [a] second [time].

en.L: then the priest shall command, and they shall wash that in which the mark [is], and he shall shut it up seven days a second [time].
en.B: the priest is to order the article with the patch washed and shut it away for another seven days.
en.R: Then the priest must have the thing with the mold washed. He must put it away for seven more days.

es.L: entonces el sacerdote mandará, y lavarán aquello en que [está] la marca, y lo encerrará siete días por segunda [vez].
es.B: el sacerdote mandará lavar el objeto que tiene la mancha y lo aislará otros siete días.
es.R: Entonces el sacerdote tiene que mandar que laven la cosa que tiene el moho. Tiene que guardarla aparte siete días más.

fr.L: alors le prêtre ordonnera, et on lavera ce dans quoi [est] la marque, et il l’enfermera sept jours une seconde [fois].
fr.B: le prêtre fera laver l’objet qui porte la tache et le mettra à l’écart encore sept jours.
fr.R: Alors le prêtre doit faire laver l’objet qui a la moisissure. Il doit le ranger à part pendant sept jours de plus.

sw.L: ndipo kuhani ataamuru, nao watakiosha kile ambacho alama [iko] ndani yake, naye atakifungia siku saba mara ya pili.
sw.B: kuhani ataagiza kitu chenye doa hilo kioshwe, naye atakitenga kwa siku nyingine saba.
sw.R: Basi lazima kuhani aagize kitu chenye ukungu kioshwe. Lazima akiweke mahali pa pekee kwa siku saba zaidi.

decisions.choice: the priest shall command, and they shall wash: others do the washing
decisions.reason: The priest gives the order and others, no doubt the owners, do the work, as in 14:36.

source.text: וְרָאָ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אַחֲרֵ֣י׀הֻכַּבֵּ֣ס אֶת־הַנֶּ֗גַע וְ֠הִנֵּה לֹֽא־הָפַ֨ךְ הַנֶּ֤גַע אֶת־עֵינוֹ֙ וְהַנֶּ֣גַע לֹֽא־פָשָׂ֔ה טָמֵ֣א ה֔וּא בָּאֵ֖שׁ תִּשְׂרְפֶ֑נּוּ פְּחֶ֣תֶת הִ֔וא בְּקָרַחְתּ֖וֹ א֥וֹ בְגַבַּחְתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will see the priest after was washed the mark, and there! not has turned the mark its eye, and the mark not has spread, unclean it [is]; with fire you will burn it; [a] rot it [is], on its back or on its front.

en.L: And the priest shall look after the mark has been washed, and there! the mark has not changed its eye, and the mark has not spread; it [is] unclean; you shall burn it with fire; it [is] a rot, on its back or on its front.
en.B: After it has been washed, the priest is to look at the patch again. If its appearance has not changed, even though it has not spread, it is unclean. You must burn it; it is a rot that has eaten into the back or the front of it.
en.R: After the thing has been washed, the priest must look at the mold again. It may look the same as before, even if it has not spread. Then the thing is unclean. You must burn it in a fire. The mold has eaten into it, on one side or the other.

es.L: Y el sacerdote mirará después de que la marca haya sido lavada, y he aquí, no ha cambiado la marca su ojo, y la marca no se ha extendido; impura [es]; con fuego la quemarás; corrosión [es], en su revés o en su derecho.
es.B: Después de lavarlo, el sacerdote volverá a examinar la mancha. Si su aspecto no ha cambiado, aunque no se haya extendido, es impuro. Tienes que quemarlo; es una corrosión que lo ha carcomido por el revés o por el derecho.
es.R: Después de lavar la cosa, el sacerdote tiene que mirar otra vez el moho. Puede que se vea igual que antes, aunque no se haya extendido. Entonces la cosa es impura. Tienes que quemarla en el fuego. El moho la ha carcomido por un lado o por el otro.

fr.L: Et le prêtre regardera après que la marque a été lavée, et voici, la marque n’a pas changé son œil, et la marque ne s’est pas étendue ; elle [est] impure ; tu la brûleras au feu ; c’[est] une corrosion, à son envers ou à son endroit.
fr.B: Après le lavage, le prêtre examinera de nouveau la tache. Si son aspect n’a pas changé, même si elle ne s’est pas étendue, l’objet est impur. Tu le brûleras ; c’est une corrosion qui l’a rongé à l’envers ou à l’endroit.
fr.R: Après le lavage, le prêtre doit regarder la moisissure encore une fois. Elle a peut-être le même aspect qu’avant, même si elle ne s’est pas étendue. Alors l’objet est impur. Tu dois le brûler dans le feu. La moisissure l’a rongé d’un côté ou de l’autre.

sw.L: Na kuhani ataangalia baada ya alama kuoshwa, na tazama, alama haijabadili jicho lake, wala alama haijaenea; ni najisi; utakichoma kwa moto; ni uozo, upande wake wa nyuma au upande wake wa mbele.
sw.B: Baada ya kuoshwa, kuhani atalichunguza doa tena. Ikiwa sura yake haijabadilika, hata kama halijaenea, kitu hicho ni najisi. Utakichoma kwa moto; ni uozo uliokila upande wa ndani au wa nje.
sw.R: Baada ya kitu hicho kuoshwa, lazima kuhani auangalie ukungu tena. Huenda unaonekana vilevile kama mwanzo, hata kama haujaenea. Basi kitu hicho ni najisi. Lazima ukichome motoni. Ukungu umekila upande mmoja au mwingine.

decisions.choice: has not changed its eye: its look has not changed
decisions.reason: 'Eye' here means appearance, as in Numbers 11:7. Washing should have made a harmless mark fade (verse 56). If it looks the same, the thing is unclean even without spreading.

decisions.choice: a rot: an eating away of the material
decisions.reason: The word appears only here. It seems to come from the root of the noun 'pit', and so to mean a hollow eaten into the fabric.

decisions.choice: on its back or on its front: on one side of the material or the other
decisions.reason: The two words are the ones used for baldness at the back of the head and at the forehead (verses 41-42). Of cloth they seem to mean the inner and outer sides, or perhaps the worn and the unworn; the blight is there either way.

decisions.choice: you
decisions.reason: Here and in verse 57 the law turns to the people as 'you'. Every level keeps it.

decisions.choice: "quemarás", "tienes que quemarla": "tú", with no plural-you span
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" here and in verses 57-58 is singular, so Spanish uses "tú" and has no plural-you setting to apply. "El revés o el derecho" are the ordinary Spanish words for the two sides of a cloth.

decisions.choice: "tu"; "à l'envers ou à l'endroit"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" here and in verses 57-58 is singular, so French says "tu". "L'envers" and "l'endroit" are the ordinary French words for the two sides of a cloth.

decisions.choice: singular "utakichoma"; "upande wa nyuma au wa mbele" (L), "upande wa ndani au wa nje" (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" here and in verses 57-58 is singular, so Swahili uses the singular "u-". Balanced says "inner or outer side", the likely sense for cloth (see m3).

source.text: וְאִם֮ רָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵן֒ וְהִנֵּה֙ כֵּהָ֣ה הַנֶּ֔גַע אַחֲרֵ֖י הֻכַּבֵּ֣ס אֹת֑וֹ וְקָרַ֣ע אֹת֗וֹ מִן־הַבֶּ֨גֶד֙ א֣וֹ מִן־הָע֔וֹר א֥וֹ מִן־הַשְּׁתִ֖י א֥וֹ מִן־הָעֵֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And if has seen the priest, and there! has grown faint the mark after it was washed, then he will tear it from the garment or from the hide or from the warp or from the woof.

en.L: But if the priest has looked, and there! the mark has grown faint after it was washed, then he shall tear it out of the garment or out of the hide or out of the warp or out of the woof.
en.B: But if the priest looks and the patch has faded after being washed, he is to tear the patch out of the clothing, the leather, or the warp or weft.
en.R: But the priest may see that the mold has become pale after the washing. Then he must tear the moldy part out of the cloth, the leather or the threads.

es.L: Pero si el sacerdote ha mirado, y he aquí, la marca se ha apagado después de haber sido lavada, la arrancará del vestido o de la piel o de la urdimbre o de la trama.
es.B: Pero si el sacerdote mira y la mancha ha perdido color después del lavado, arrancará la mancha de la ropa, del cuero, o de la urdimbre o la trama.
es.R: Pero puede que el sacerdote vea que el moho se ha puesto pálido después del lavado. Entonces tiene que arrancar la parte con moho de la tela, del cuero o de los hilos.

fr.L: Mais si le prêtre a regardé, et voici, la marque est devenue terne après avoir été lavée, il l’arrachera du vêtement ou de la peau ou de la chaîne ou de la trame.
fr.B: Mais si le prêtre constate que la tache a pâli après le lavage, il arrachera la tache du vêtement, du cuir, ou de la chaîne ou de la trame.
fr.R: Mais le prêtre peut voir que la moisissure est devenue pâle après le lavage. Alors il doit arracher la partie moisie du tissu, du cuir ou des fils.

sw.L: Lakini kuhani akiwa ameangalia, na tazama, alama imefifia baada ya kuoshwa, ataichana kutoka katika vazi au katika ngozi au katika mtande au katika mshindio.
sw.B: Lakini kuhani akichunguza na kuona kwamba doa limefifia baada ya kuoshwa, atalichana doa hilo litoke katika nguo, ngozi, au mtande au mshindio.
sw.R: Lakini huenda kuhani akaona kwamba ukungu umepauka baada ya kuoshwa. Basi lazima achane sehemu yenye ukungu iondoke katika kitambaa, ngozi au nyuzi.

decisions.choice: tear it out: remove only the marked part
decisions.reason: Only the marked piece is removed. The rest may be kept, unless the mark comes back (verses 57-58).

source.text: וְאִם־תֵּרָאֶ֨ה ע֜וֹד בַּ֠בֶּגֶד אֽוֹ־בַשְּׁתִ֤י אֽוֹ־בָעֵ֨רֶב֙ א֣וֹ בְכָל־כְּלִי־ע֔וֹר פֹּרַ֖חַת הִ֑וא בָּאֵ֣שׁ תִּשְׂרְפֶ֔נּוּ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־בּ֖וֹ הַנָּֽגַע׃

records.literal_gloss: And if it will appear again in the garment or in the warp or in the woof or in any article of hide, breaking out it [is]; with fire you will burn it, [that] which the mark [is] in.
